definition_zh: 摩托车；轻便摩托车；机动自行车
definition_en: a two-wheeled vehicle powered by an engine, especially a light one; also a bicycle fitted with a small engine
core_image: 一辆两轮车靠在墙边，座垫上扣着一顶旧头盔
scene: 雨后的巷口，一辆两轮小车贴墙停着，座位被雨水打得发亮。 He left his motorbike by the wall and wiped the seat with a cloth.
sceneCN: 这里是「摩托车」（第 1 个义项：以发动机驱动的两轮车）；句意为他把摩托车停在墙边，用布擦了擦座垫。图中可辨识物件：两轮车、墙壁、湿漉漉的座垫。

pos.zh: 摩托车；轻便摩托车；机动自行车

senses.title: A two-wheeled machine driven by an engine
senses.definition: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine, ridden by one or two people
senses.definitionCN: 装有发动机、由一两个人骑乘的两轮道路车辆
senses.example: He left his motorbike by the wall and wiped the seat with a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他把摩托车停在墙边，用布擦了擦座垫。
senses.why: The word is a plain compound of motor and bike, so it names the thing by its two parts: an engine plus a bicycle frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 motor 与 bike 直接复合而成，所以它用两个部件给东西命名：一台发动机加一副自行车车架。

senses.title: A light motorcycle for short trips
senses.definition: a small, light motorcycle, the kind often used for short journeys in town
senses.definitionCN: 车身轻、排量小的摩托车，多用于城里短途出行
senses.example: She bought a small motorbike for the two-mile ride to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一辆轻便摩托车，用来骑到两英里外的车站。
senses.why: Because the compound says nothing about size, British speakers use it most often for the small machines that replace a bicycle, and the light sense grew from that habit rather than from the word's form.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个复合词本身不交代大小，英式说法最常拿它指替代自行车的那种小机器，「轻便」这一层意思是从用法习惯里长出来的，而不是词形自带。

senses.title: A bicycle with a small engine added
senses.definition: a bicycle to which a small engine has been fitted, common where fuel is cheap and distances are short
senses.definitionCN: 在自行车上加装小发动机的两轮车，在油价便宜、路途很短的地方常见
senses.example: In the village, a motorbike with pedals was cheaper than a car.
senses.exampleCN: 在村里，一辆带脚踏的机动自行车比汽车便宜。
senses.why: Bike itself means bicycle, so the compound can still be read literally: a bicycle with a motor attached, a reading that survives where such machines are everyday transport.
senses.whyCN: bike 本身是自行车的简称，所以这个复合词仍可照字面读成「装了发动机的自行车」；在那种机器就是日常交通工具的地方，这个读法一直活着。

intro.en: Motorbike joins two ordinary English nouns, motor and bike, and the compound is generally dated to the late nineteenth century, when engine-driven two-wheelers appeared.
intro.cn: motorbike 把 motor 与 bike 两个普通英语名词合在一起，一般认为这个复合词出现于十九世纪后期，正当发动机驱动的两轮车登场。

items.en: The first half goes back to Latin motor, a mover, by way of the English noun motor, the engine that drives a machine.
items.cn: 前半部分可追到拉丁语 motor（推动者），再经英语名词 motor（驱动机器的发动机）而来。

items.en: Bike is a nineteenth-century shortening of bicycle, coined when the pedal-driven two-wheeler became common.
items.cn: bike 是十九世纪 bicycle 的缩略，在脚踏驱动的两轮车普及之时造出。

items.en: Motor and bike were joined as motorbike in the late nineteenth century, a step generally taken to follow the arrival of engine-driven two-wheelers.
items.cn: motor 与 bike 在十九世纪后期合成 motorbike，一般认为这一步跟随发动机驱动两轮车的出现。

items.en: British English adopted motorbike as its everyday word for a motorcycle, while American English usually keeps the longer motorcycle.
items.cn: 英式英语把 motorbike 收作摩托车的日常说法，而美式英语通常仍用较长的 motorcycle。

items.en: Modern English also applies the word to bicycles fitted with small engines, so it now covers both the road machine and the assisted bicycle.
items.cn: 现代英语也用它指加装小发动机的自行车，这个词如今同时涵盖公路上的摩托车与助力自行车。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two halves of the compound and the vehicles built on them; the near-meaning group collects the two-wheeled machines it is often compared with.
note.cn: 形近组顺着复合词的两个部件以及由它们构成的车辆展开；近义组收常与它比较的两轮车。

normalIntro.en: Two everyday nouns sit inside this compound, and the family that surrounds it keeps naming the machine, its rider and the activity of riding it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词里装着两个日常名词，围绕它的词族则不断给机器、骑车人和骑车这件事命名。

normal.en: Motor supplies the engine half and bike the frame half, so the compound is a description as much as a name.
normal.cn: motor 提供发动机这一半，bike 提供车架这一半，所以这个复合词既是名字，也是一句描述。

normal.en: Bike is a shortening of bicycle, which is bi- for two plus the Greek word for wheel, so the second half literally says two wheels.
normal.cn: bike 是 bicycle 的缩略，而 bicycle 是 bi-（二）加希腊语「轮子」，所以后半部分字面上就在说「两个轮子」。

normal.en: Motorcycle is the longer, more formal twin, and it is the usual word in American English where motorbike sounds distinctly British.
normal.cn: motorcycle 是更长、更正式的那个对应词，在美式英语里通常用它，而 motorbike 听起来明显是英式说法。

normal.en: Motorist and motorcyclist both add a person suffix to the machine name, turning a vehicle into a word for its rider.
normal.cn: motorist 与 motorcyclist 都在机器名后加表示人的词尾，把车辆变成骑车人的说法。

normal.en: The same word covers the road motorcycle and the assisted bicycle because bike keeps its bicycle sense inside the compound.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指公路上的摩托车，也指助力自行车，因为 bike 在复合词里保留着「自行车」那一层意思。

abstract.en: Picture a bicycle frame with a small engine bolted into the middle, a machine that is half pedal and half piston.
abstract.cn: 想象一副自行车车架，中间焊上一台小发动机，一半是脚踏，一半是活塞。

abstract.en: A compound that simply stacks two everyday words shows that English often names a new machine by naming the old ones it joins.
abstract.cn: 一个把两个日常词叠起来的复合词说明，英语常用「把被合并的两样旧东西说出来」的方式给新机器命名。

abstract.en: The British preference for the short word and the American preference for the long one is a reminder that vocabulary carries address as well as meaning.
abstract.cn: 英式偏爱短词、美式偏爱长词，这提醒人：词汇不只携带意义，也携带口音里的地域。

去掉否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「可被战胜的」
同带 vinc- 词根的形近词，义为「说服」

senses.title: Undefeated in battle
senses.definition: so strong that no enemy can defeat it
senses.definitionCN: 强大到没有任何敌人能够击败
senses.example: For a century the fortress was thought invincible.
senses.exampleCN: 一个世纪里，这座要塞都被认为攻不破。
senses.why: Latin vincere meant "to conquer", and in- here simply negates it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vincere 意为「征服」，这里的 in- 只是把它否定掉。

senses.title: Unbeatable in a contest
senses.definition: performing so well that rivals cannot win against you
senses.definitionCN: 表现好到对手无法取胜
senses.example: The chess champion seemed invincible until a schoolgirl beat him.
senses.exampleCN: 这位象棋冠军似乎无人能敌，直到一个女学生赢了他。
senses.why: Sport and games borrowed the military word whenever a record held.
senses.whyCN: 体育与游戏在纪录无人打破时就借来这个军事词。

senses.title: Unshakable in feeling
senses.definition: too firm in courage or belief to be weakened by setbacks
senses.definitionCN: 勇气或信念坚定到挫折也无法削弱
senses.example: She went into the hearing with invincible calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着不可动摇的镇定走进听证会。
senses.why: The word moved from the body to the mind: what cannot be beaten inside is also invincible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身体挪到心灵：内里打不败的东西也是无敌的。

intro.en: Invincible is the Latin negative in- joined to vincibilis, "able to be overcome".
intro.cn: invincible 是拉丁否定前缀 in- 加上 vincibilis「可被战胜的」。

items.en: vincere meant "to conquer, to prevail".
items.cn: vincere 意为「征服、取胜」。

items.en: The adjective vincibilis meant "can be overcome".
items.cn: 形容词 vincibilis 意为「可被战胜的」。

items.en: Adding in- produced invincibilis, "not to be overcome".
items.cn: 加 in- 构成 invincibilis「不可战胜的」。

items.en: French passed the word on as invincible.
items.cn: 法语以 invincible 把它传出。

items.en: English applied it to armies first, then to minds and arguments.
items.cn: 英语先用它说军队，后来说心志与论点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vinc- root; the near-meaning group holds words for being unbeatable.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vinc- 词根；近义组收表示不可击败的词。

entries.definition: To make someone believe something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「说服」，同词根。

entries.definition: Able to be defeated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「可战胜的」，少了否定前缀。

entries.definition: Impossible to see.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「看不见的」，只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Impossible to beat in a contest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「无法击败的」，偏口语。

entries.definition: Never to be taken by force.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不可征服的」，偏书面。

entries.definition: Spirit that cannot be tamed or broken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不屈不挠的」，多指精神。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into a no plus a conquer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它拆成一个「不」加一个「征服」。

normal.en: in- means not, and vinc- means conquer.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，vinc- 是「征服」。

normal.en: Invincible is literally unconquerable.
normal.cn: invincible 字面上就是不可征服。

normal.en: Take off in- and you get vincible, which no army wants.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 就得到 vincible，没有军队想当。

normal.en: Winners in one long season get called invincible.
normal.cn: 连赢一整个赛季的队伍就被叫无敌。

normal.en: Vinc- also hides in convince, where you conquer a doubt.
normal.cn: vinc- 也藏在 convince 里，征服的是怀疑。

abstract.en: Invincibility is a mirror that only looks one way.
abstract.cn: 无敌是一面只朝一个方向照的镜子。

abstract.en: A shield with no scratch is also a shield with no story.
abstract.cn: 没有划痕的盾，也没有故事。

abstract.en: The calm that cannot be shaken is the quiet kind of victory.
abstract.cn: 摇不动的镇定，是安静的一种胜利。

examples.en: No army is truly invincible, however many battles it wins.
examples.cn: 无论赢多少场仗，没有军队真能无敌。

examples.en: The old champion looked invincible until the second round.
examples.cn: 那位老冠军看起来无人能敌，直到第二轮就败了。

examples.en: She faced the crowd with invincible confidence.
examples.cn: 她以不可动摇的自信面对人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vinc（征服）+ ible（能……的）——没能被征服的

root: 拉丁语 vincere「征服」→ vincibilis「可被战胜的」→ 加否定前缀 in- 成 invincibilis → 英语 invincible。同族有 vincible、invincibility、convince。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: undefeated in war, unbeatable in competition, and unshakable in spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：战场不可战胜、比赛无人能胜，以及精神上不可动摇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shield that takes every blow and shows no mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：挨了所有打击却毫无痕迹的盾牌。

branches.en: THE FORTRESS: walls no siege can break.
branches.cn: 要塞这条线：围城攻不破的墙。

branches.en: THE STREAK: a record that keeps holding.
branches.cn: 连胜这条线：一直没人打破的纪录。

branches.en: THE NERVE: courage that setbacks cannot dent.
branches.cn: 心志这条线：挫折也压不垮的勇气。

branches.en: THE TEST: both senses are judged by someone attacking.
branches.cn: 考验这条线：两个义项都要有人来攻才显出来。

branches.en: THE REVIEW: rivals and doubts are the same kind of pressure.
branches.cn: 审视这条线：对手与怀疑是同一种压力。

intro.en: Invincible is in- "not" plus vinc- "conquer" plus -ible "able to be".
intro.cn: invincible 是 in-「不」加 vinc-「征服」再加 -ible「能被……的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vincere and invincibilis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vincere 与 invincibilis 均有记载。

items.example: It flips the meaning of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词的意思翻过来。

items.example: The root also appears in convince.
It forms vincible, able to be beaten.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 vincible，能被战胜的。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: A cousin of the same root with a different spelling.
items.exampleCN: 同词根的表亲，拼写略异。

items.example: Here the conquering happens inside another mind.
items.exampleCN: 在这里，征服发生在别人的脑子里。

definition_zh: 重新开始；续订；延长；更新；恢复
definition_en: to begin something again, or to make something valid or fresh once more
core_image: 枯枝上重新冒出的一层新绿
scene: 护照还有一个月到期，他赶在出发前去重新办理。 His passport expires next month, so he went to renew it before the trip.
sceneCN: 这里 renew 是「续办、延期」（第 2 个义项：延长证件的有效期）；句意：他的护照下个月到期，所以出发前去续办了。

pos.zh: 重新开始；续订；延长；更新；恢复

derivatives.zh: renew 加 -al 构成，义为「更新；续订」
renew 加 -able 构成，义为「可再生的；可续期的」
renew 加 -ed 构成，义为「重新焕发的」

senses.title: To begin something again
senses.definition: to start an activity or a relationship again after a pause
senses.definitionCN: 在停顿之后重新开始某项活动或关系
senses.example: The two countries agreed to renew talks next month.
senses.exampleCN: 两国同意下月重启谈判。
senses.why: The word is simply re- plus new, so the core image is something old putting out fresh growth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 re- 加 new，所以核心画面是旧枝上重新长出新芽。

senses.title: To extend something that expires
senses.definition: to arrange for a document, contract, or subscription to stay valid for longer
senses.definitionCN: 安排证件、合同或订阅继续有效更长时间
senses.example: She renewed her library books online.
senses.exampleCN: 她在网上续借了图书馆的书。
senses.why: Making a thing new again in time is the administrative version of the same renewal.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上让某物重新变新，就是行政意义上的续期。

senses.title: To replace with something new
senses.definition: to put a new part or version in place of an old one
senses.definitionCN: 用新的部件或版本替换旧的
senses.example: The old pipes were renewed last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 旧管道去年夏天全部换新了。
senses.why: The plain sense of making new becomes physical replacement in buildings and equipment.
senses.whyCN: 「使变新」在建筑与设备上落实为实物的更换。

senses.title: To restore strength or feeling
senses.definition: to give someone fresh energy, hope, or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 给某人新的精力、希望或信心
senses.example: A short rest renewed his confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 短暂的休息让他重拾信心。
senses.why: A tired body or a low spirit can also be made new, which is the emotional sense.
senses.whyCN: 疲惫的身体或低落的心情同样可以「变新」，这就是精神层面的义项。

intro.en: Renew is an English formation of re- and the native adjective new, first recorded in the late fourteenth century.
intro.cn: renew 是英语中由前缀 re- 与本土形容词 new 构成的词，最早见于十四世纪晚期。

items.en: The adjective niwe means new, and becomes modern English new.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 niwe 意为「新的」，后来演变为现代英语的 new。

items.en: The parallel French verb renouveler may have supported the English formation.
items.cn: 法语中平行的动词 renouveler 可能对英语构词起了推动作用。

items.en: Renew first means to resume or begin again.
items.cn: renew 最初意为恢复或重新开始。

items.en: The word extends to replacing worn parts and to extending documents in time.
items.cn: 词义扩展到更换磨损部件以及延长文书的有效期。

items.en: Renewable becomes a key word for energy sources that nature replaces.
items.cn: renewable 成为指代自然界可再补充的能源的关键词。

note.en: Renew is a transparent compound of re- and new, and it stands near words for restoring and for extending.
note.cn: renew 是 re- 与 new 的透明复合词，与表示恢复和延长的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of making something new or valid again
entries.definitionCN: 更新；续订，由 renew 加 -al 构成

entries.definition: able to be replaced naturally or extended
entries.definitionCN: 可再生的；可续期的

entries.definition: recently made or not existing before
entries.definitionCN: 新的，是 renew 的本土词根

entries.definition: to bring something back to an earlier good state
entries.definitionCN: 恢复；修复，强调回到原状

entries.definition: to make something last longer
entries.definitionCN: 延长，与第二义项接近

entries.definition: to begin again after a break
entries.definitionCN: 重新开始；继续，与第一义项接近

normalIntro.en: Renew is re- plus the native word new, which makes the meaning almost visible.
normalIntro.cn: renew 就是 re- 加本土词 new，意思几乎一眼可见。

normal.en: Re- plus new means to make new again, in time, in matter, or in spirit.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 new，就是在时间、物质或精神上重新变新。

normal.en: Add -al for renewal and -able for renewable.
normal.cn: 加 -al 得 renewal，加 -able 得 renewable。

normal.en: Renewable energy is energy that nature keeps replacing.
normal.cn: renewable energy 指自然界不断补充的能源。

normal.en: Renew a passport, a contract, and a subscription are the three practical collocations.
normal.cn: renew a passport、renew a contract、renew a subscription 是三个实用搭配。

normal.en: The past participle renewed often works as an adjective meaning fresh again.
normal.cn: 过去分词 renewed 常用作形容词，表示「重新焕发的」。

abstract.en: Picture green shoots pushing out of a bare branch in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象春天枯枝上冒出嫩绿的新芽。

abstract.en: See a stamped page in a passport being replaced by a new one.
abstract.cn: 想象护照上一页印章被换成了新的一页。

abstract.en: Think of a tired runner standing up after a cup of water.
abstract.cn: 想一位疲惫的跑者喝完一杯水后重新站起。

examples.en: We need to renew the lease before June.
examples.cn: 我们得在六月之前续签租约。

examples.en: The rain renewed the garden after a dry month.
examples.cn: 干旱一个月后，这场雨让花园重新焕发生机。

examples.en: They met again and renewed their friendship.
examples.cn: 他们再次相见，重续了友谊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞牛」——想象瑞丽的牛经过一冬又长出新毛，焕然一新；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 re-（再次）加形容词 new（新的），字面即「使重新变新」。

sensesIntro.en: Making something new again applies to time, to a document, to worn material, and to a tired spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: 「使重新变新」分别施加于时间、文书、磨损的材料以及疲惫的精神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fresh green shoots on a bare branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：枯枝上重新冒出的新绿。

branches.en: Starting again after a pause is the temporal sense.
branches.cn: 停顿之后重新开始，是时间层面的义项。

branches.en: Pushing an expiry date forward is renewal in administration.
branches.cn: 把有效期往后推，是行政层面的更新。

branches.en: Swapping old parts for new is renewal in matter.
branches.cn: 用新部件换掉旧的，是物质层面的更新。

branches.en: Refilling energy or hope is renewal in spirit.
branches.cn: 重新注入精力或希望，是精神层面的更新。

branches.en: Both restart something that had stopped or faded.
branches.cn: 两者都让已经停下或消退的东西重新开始。

intro.en: Renew is one of the clearest prefix-plus-word compounds in English, with a Latin prefix on a native base.
intro.cn: renew 是英语中最清晰的「前缀加单词」复合词之一，拉丁前缀加在本土词根上。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and new is the native English adjective for something recently made.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再次」，new 是英语本族形容词，表示「新近形成的」。

items.example: Re- repeats the making of something new.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示把「变新」再做一次。

items.example: New is the native base of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: new 是整个词的本土基础。

items.example: Niwe is the Old English form of new.
items.exampleCN: niwe 是 new 的古英语形式。

items.example: Renewal names the act of renewing.
Renewable means able to be renewed.
items.exampleCN: renewable 意为「可以被更新的」。

items.example: Renewed confidence is confidence that has come back.
items.exampleCN: renewed confidence 指重新回来的信心。

items.meaning: the process of making new again
items.exampleCN: urban renewal 指旧城区的改造复兴。

items.example: Renouveler is the parallel French formation.
items.exampleCN: renouveler 是法语中平行的构词。

definition_zh: 不必要的；多余的；无谓的
definition_en: not needed, or more than is needed
core_image: 桌上已经堆满杯子，有人又端来一只
scene: 搬家那天车里最后一个空位塞满了纸箱，朋友们却还想把旧花盆也搬上去。 Bringing that old pot along is quite unnecessary.
sceneCN: 这里 unnecessary 是「不必要的」（第 1 个义项：用不着、多此一举）；句意为把那只旧花盆带上其实完全没有必要。桌上多出杯子的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不必要地；多余地」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「必要的；必需的」
同根名词，义为「必要；必需品」
同根动词，义为「使成为必要」

senses.title: Not needed for a purpose
senses.definition: not required, because the purpose can be achieved without it
senses.definitionCN: 不需要的，因为不用它也能达到目的
senses.example: Another copy of the report is unnecessary, since we already have two.
senses.exampleCN: 报告再印一份没必要，我们已经有两份了。
senses.why: The prefix says not, and the base word names what cannot be done without; so the whole word names what can be done without.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根指「离不开的东西」；合在一起就是「不用它也行」的东西。

senses.title: More than the situation calls for
senses.definition: extra, beyond what a situation needs or deserves
senses.definitionCN: 多出来的，超出情境所需或应有的限度
senses.example: He was asked to cut the unnecessary detail from the report.
senses.exampleCN: 他被要求删掉报告里多余的细节。
senses.why: Once a thing is not needed, anything beyond it becomes surplus, and this surplus sense grows straight out of the core image.
senses.whyCN: 既然用不着，那么超出所需的部分自然就成了多余之物，这层「过量」义正是从核心意象长出来的。

senses.title: Risk that could have been avoided
senses.definition: used of a risk or danger that could easily be avoided
senses.definitionCN: 形容本来很容易避免的风险或危险
senses.example: Driving after midnight was an unnecessary risk.
senses.exampleCN: 半夜开车是无谓的冒险。
senses.why: A person adds what is not needed and thereby adds danger; the word then attaches to the danger itself.
senses.whyCN: 人加了用不着的东西，也就多添了危险；于是这个词也用在了危险本身上。

senses.title: Words or actions that make things worse
senses.definition: used of a remark or move that causes trouble without helping
senses.definitionCN: 形容带来麻烦却毫无帮助的话语或举动
senses.example: His remark about her accent was unnecessary and hurt her.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿她的口音说事，那句话既多余又伤人。
senses.why: Speech that adds nothing is the same surplus as an extra cup on a full table, and here the surplus costs someone pain.
senses.whyCN: 对事情毫无帮助的话，就跟满桌之上再添一只杯子一样多余，只是这一次多余还让别人受了伤。

senses.title: Unlike what one would expect in logic
senses.definition: used in logic and argument for a condition that is not required for the result
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与论证中指对结论并不构成必需的条件
senses.example: The third assumption is unnecessary for the proof to hold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明的成立并不需要第三条假设。
senses.why: Strip away everything a result does not require, and what remains is exactly what unnecessary means in logic.
senses.whyCN: 把一个结论所不需要的东西全部剥掉，剩下的正是逻辑上所说的「非必需」。

intro.en: A simple English compound: the negative prefix un- over an adjective borrowed from Latin through French.
intro.cn: 一个简单的英语复合词：否定前缀 un- 加在经由法语借入的拉丁系形容词之上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and marks the opposite of a word.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，用来表示一个词的反面。

items.en: Necessarius meant unavoidable or pressing, from necesse, that which cannot be otherwise.
items.cn: necessarius 意为「不可避免的、紧迫的」，源自 necesse（别无他法之事）。

items.en: The adjective came into French as necessaire and was attached to ordinary needs.
items.cn: 这个词以 necessaire 的形式进入法语，用于日常所需之物。

items.en: Necessary enters English in the fourteenth century and takes the negative prefix shortly after.
items.cn: necessary 于十四世纪进入英语，随后很快加上否定前缀。

items.en: Unnecessary also settles into logic and style manuals, where it labels what a proof or a sentence does not require.
items.cn: unnecessary 后来又进入逻辑学与写作手册，用来标出证明或句子不需要的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same necesse stem, and the near-meaning group collects surplus words.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一个 necesse 词干上的各种形式，近义组汇集表示多余过剩的词。

entries.definition: needed for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 必要的；必需的

entries.definition: in a way that is not needed
entries.definitionCN: 不必要地；多余地

entries.definition: something that cannot be done without
entries.definitionCN: 必需品；必要

entries.definition: to make something necessary
entries.definitionCN: 使成为必要

entries.definition: no longer needed because there is already enough
entries.definitionCN: 多余的；冗余的

entries.definition: more than is wanted or required
entries.definitionCN: 过剩的；多余的

entries.definition: possible but not required
entries.definitionCN: 可选的；非必需的

entries.definition: completely necessary
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的

normalIntro.en: The word is transparent: a negative prefix laid over the everyday word for what cannot be done without.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词十分透明：一个否定前缀压在日常表示「离不开」的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus necessary: what is not necessary is unnecessary.
normal.cn: un- 加 necessary：不是必需的，就是 unnecessary。

normal.en: It is unnecessary to do something is the standard sentence frame.
normal.cn: it is unnecessary to do 是标准句型框架。

normal.en: The adverb unnecessarily often appears with verbs of complaining and spending.
normal.cn: 副词 unnecessarily 常与抱怨、花费类动词连用。

normal.en: Necessary, necessity, and necessitate all share the Latin stem necesse.
normal.cn: necessary、necessity、necessitate 共享拉丁词干 necesse。

normal.en: Formal writing prefers unnecessary to unneeded.
normal.cn: 正式写作里更常用 unnecessary 而不是 unneeded。

abstract.en: See a third cup placed on a table that already holds two.
abstract.cn: 想象一张已有两只杯子的桌上又放下第三只。

abstract.en: Hear a joke told twice, then a long silence.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话被讲了两遍，然后是一阵长久的沉默。

abstract.en: Feel a suitcase that will not close because someone packed for a longer trip.
abstract.cn: 体会一只因有人按更长的旅程收拾而合不上的行李箱。

examples.en: The extra meeting was unnecessary, since everyone had already agreed.
examples.cn: 那次额外会议没必要，因为大家早已达成一致。

examples.en: Staying until midnight was an unnecessary risk, and she regretted it.
examples.cn: 待到半夜是无谓的冒险，她后来很后悔。

examples.en: The editor removed every unnecessary word from the paragraph.
examples.cn: 编辑删掉了这一段里每一个多余的词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必需品」——东西已经够了还往包里塞，多带的那些俺自己也知道用不着。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ necessary（必需的），necessary 源自拉丁语 necessarius / necesse（不是别的选择、无法避免），经古法语 necessaire 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: From one core point, what can be done without, the word spreads to surplus, needless risk, useless remarks, and logic.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个核心点「不用它也行」出发，这个词扩展到多余、无谓风险、无用之言与逻辑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more cup on an already full table.
core.cn: 核心意象：已经摆满的桌上又放下一只杯子。

branches.en: The plain branch: the job is done without it.
branches.cn: 朴素分支：不用它事情照样办成。

branches.en: The surplus branch: more than the situation allows for.
branches.cn: 过剩分支：超出情境所需的部分。

branches.en: The risk branch: danger added for no gain.
branches.cn: 风险分支：毫无收益地添上的危险。

branches.en: The remark branch: words that add nothing and hurt.
branches.cn: 言语分支：毫无帮助还伤人的话。

branches.en: The logic branch: a condition the proof never uses.
branches.cn: 逻辑分支：证明从未用到的条件。

intro.en: A Germanic negative prefix plus a borrowed adjective whose own parts are easy to read.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语否定前缀，加上一个部件清晰的借入形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem is necesse, that which cannot be otherwise, with the adjective ending -arius.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干为 necesse（别无他法之事），加上形容词词尾 -arius。

items.meaningCN: 在 necesse 中表示否定的成分
items.example: Necesse is built on an old negative element.
items.exampleCN: necesse 由古老的否定成分构成。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词后缀

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可避免的；别无他法的
不可避免的；不可或缺的

definition_zh: 好奇地；奇怪地
definition_en: in a way that shows a wish to know, or in a strange way
core_image: 一个人歪着头，慢慢凑近看一样东西
scene: 他歪着头，慢慢把脸凑近那枚旧硬币。 She looked curiously at the small door in the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 curiously 指「好奇地」（第 1 个义项：带着想知道的兴趣）；句意是她好奇地看着墙上的那扇小门。

senses.title: In a curious way
senses.definition: with a strong wish to know or see more
senses.definitionCN: 带着强烈想知道或看更多的愿望
senses.example: He looked curiously at the old map.
senses.exampleCN: 他好奇地看着那张旧地图。
senses.why: The body leans in when the mind wants more.
senses.whyCN: 心里想要更多时，身体会往前倾。

senses.title: Strangely
senses.definition: in a way that seems strange or hard to explain
senses.definitionCN: 以显得奇怪或难以解释的方式
senses.example: The room was curiously quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里安静得奇怪。
senses.why: A thing can be odd in how it behaves, not just in how it looks.
senses.whyCN: 事物的古怪，可能在它的举止，而不只在样子。

senses.title: With care, in older use
senses.definition: with care and skill, in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 旧文字中指用心而有技艺地
senses.example: The box was curiously carved.
senses.exampleCN: 这只箱子雕刻得十分精细。
senses.why: Care shows in small repeated cuts.
senses.whyCN: 用心显在一刀刀细小的刻痕里。

intro.en: Curiously is curious plus -ly; curious comes from Latin curiosus, from cura, care.
intro.cn: curiously 由 curious 加 -ly 构成；curious 源自拉丁语 curiosus，其根是 cura（关心）。

items.en: Cura meant care and attention.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与用心。

items.en: Curiosus meant careful and eager to know.
items.cn: curiosus 意为用心的、急于知道的。

items.en: Curious meant careful and skillful.
items.cn: curious 意为细心而有技艺的。

items.en: Curious settled into eager to know and strange.
items.cn: curious 固定为好奇的与奇怪的。

items.en: The adverb curiously followed the adjective.
items.cn: 副词 curiously 随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the curi- stem, and the meaning group names other adverbs of manner and oddness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 curi- 词干，近义组列出其他表示方式与古怪的副词。

entries.definition: wanting to know something
entries.definitionCN: 想知道某事的

entries.definition: the wish to know something
entries.definitionCN: 想了解某事的愿望

entries.definition: the state of being curious
entries.definitionCN: 好奇的状态

entries.definition: in an unusual way
entries.definitionCN: 以不寻常的方式

entries.definition: in a way that seems odd
entries.definitionCN: 以显得古怪的方式

entries.definition: in a questioning way
entries.definitionCN: 带着追问的方式

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a tilted head and end with a strangely quiet room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从歪着的头开始，落到一间安静得奇怪的房间。

normal.en: Curiously is how the body moves when the mind asks.
normal.cn: curiously 就是心里发问时身体的动法。

normal.en: A head tilts before a question is spoken.
normal.cn: 问题出口前，头先歪过去。

normal.en: An old map can hold a person for an hour.
normal.cn: 一张旧地图能留住一个人一小时。

normal.en: The same word says a room is oddly quiet.
normal.cn: 同一个词也说房间安静得奇怪。

normal.en: Add -ly and the looking becomes a manner.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly，看就变成了一种方式。

abstract.en: Picture an eye moving closer to a small coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼睛凑近一枚小硬币。

abstract.en: Picture fingers turning a page very slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象手指很慢地翻过一页。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that ticks too softly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只走得过于轻的钟。

examples.en: She looked curiously at the stranger.
examples.cn: 她好奇地看着那个陌生人。

examples.en: The street was curiously empty at noon.
examples.cn: 中午的街道空得奇怪。

examples.en: He asked curiously how the trick worked.
examples.cn: 他好奇地问这戏法是怎么回事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curiously 记成「带着问号地」：curious 是好奇，加上 -ly，就成了好奇地或奇怪地。

root: 由 curious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；curious 源自拉丁语 curiosus（用心的、爱探究的），其根是 cura（关心），因此 curiously 兼有「好奇地」与「奇怪地」两义。

sensesIntro.en: From a look that wants more, to a manner that seems odd, to older work done with care.
sensesIntro.cn: 从想要更多的目光，到显得古怪的举止，再到旧时精细的手艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a head tilted, an eye moving closer to an object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个歪着的头，一只越凑越近的眼睛。

branches.en: The manner shows a mind that wants more.
branches.cn: 这种方式显出想要更多的心。

branches.en: The same manner can make a thing seem odd.
branches.cn: 同一种方式，也能让事物显得古怪。

branches.en: Older writing used it for work done with care.
branches.cn: 较早的文字用它形容用心做出的活。

branches.en: Wanting to know and finding things odd sit close together.
branches.cn: 想了解与觉得古怪挨得很近。

branches.en: A carefully made thing can look strange to untrained eyes.
branches.cn: 精细之物在外行眼里可能显得奇怪。

intro.en: Curiously is the adverb built on curious, inside the large Latin cura family.
intro.cn: curiously 是由 curious 构成的副词，属于庞大的拉丁语 cura 一族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cura, care, travels through curiosus into curious and curiously.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura（关心）经 curiosus 进入 curious 与 curiously。

items.example: He glanced incuriously at the page.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无好奇地瞥了一眼那页。

items.example: A curio stood on the desk.

definition_zh: 学者
definition_en: a person who studies a subject deeply, especially at a university
core_image: 一位学者伏在堆满古籍的书桌前，专注地做着批注
scene: 这位学者用十年时间研究古文字。 The scholar spent ten years studying ancient scripts.
sceneCN: 这里 scholar 是「学者」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这位学者花了十年研究古文字。

senses.title: Deep researcher
senses.definition: a person who studies a subject deeply, especially at a university
senses.definitionCN: 深入研究某一学科的人，尤指在大学中
senses.example: Scholars still debate the meaning of the text.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们仍在争论这段文字的含义。
senses.why: The core sense is a person devoted to deep study.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是致力于深入研究的人。

senses.title: Prize student
senses.definition: a student who receives money to support study
senses.definitionCN: 获得资助以支持学业的学生
senses.example: She is a scholar at the local college.
senses.exampleCN: 她是当地学院的奖学金学生。
senses.why: Support for study names the student who receives it.
senses.whyCN: 对学业的资助以其获得者的名称来表达。

senses.title: Learned person
senses.definition: a person with great knowledge gained from reading and study
senses.definitionCN: 通过阅读和研究获得渊博知识的人
senses.example: The old scholar knew several ancient languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老学者懂好几门古代语言。
senses.why: Deep study becomes a general mark of learning.
senses.whyCN: 深入研究成为博学的普遍标志。

intro.en: Scholar comes from Latin schola, school, through Late Latin scholaris.
intro.cn: scholar 经晚期拉丁语 scholaris 源自拉丁语 schola（学校）。

items.en: Skholē meant leisure used for learning.
items.cn: skholē 意为用于学习的闲暇。

items.en: Schola meant a school or a learned discussion.
items.cn: schola 意为学校或学术讨论。

items.en: Scholaris meant of a school or a student.
items.cn: scholaris 意为学校的或学生的。

items.en: Escoler named a pupil or a learned man.
items.cn: escoler 指学生或有学问的人。

items.en: Scoler meant a student and later a learned person.
items.cn: scoler 指学生，后指博学之人。

items.en: Scholar means a specialist researcher or prize student.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scholar 指专业研究者或奖学金学生。

note.en: Scholar is compared with similar spellings and with words for learned people.
note.cn: 把 scholar 与形近词以及表示有学问之人的词作比较。

entries.definition: relating to the sun
entries.definitionCN: 太阳的

entries.definition: having size but not direction
entries.definitionCN: 标量的

entries.definition: a person who frowns angrily
entries.definitionCN: 怒视者

entries.definition: a university teacher or researcher
entries.definitionCN: 大学教师；学者

entries.definition: a person who studies a subject
entries.definitionCN: 研究者

entries.definition: a person who thinks deeply about ideas
entries.definitionCN: 知识分子

normalIntro.en: Scholar and school share the same Latin root.
normalIntro.cn: scholar 与 school 共享同一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: Scholar begins like school, because a scholar studies there.
normal.cn: scholar 开头像 school，因为学者在学校研究。

normal.en: A scholar of history studies the past deeply.
normal.cn: a scholar of history 指深入研究历史的学者。

normal.en: A visiting scholar comes to teach and learn for a time.
normal.cn: 访问学者短期来讲学和研究。

normal.en: Scholarship is the money or the learning a scholar gains.
normal.cn: scholarship 既是奖学金也是学者的学问。

normal.en: Scholarly writing is careful and full of sources.
normal.cn: 学术写作严谨且引用丰富。

abstract.en: A scholar turns curiosity into patient work.
abstract.cn: 学者把好奇心变成耐心的研究工作。

abstract.en: The word once meant leisure, because learning needs time.
abstract.cn: 这个词原意指闲暇，因为学习需要时间。

abstract.en: A scholar keeps asking even after an answer is found.
abstract.cn: 即使找到答案，学者仍继续追问。

examples.en: Scholars from many countries attended the conference.
examples.cn: 来自许多国家的学者参加了会议。

examples.en: She became a scholar of ancient languages.
examples.cn: 她成为研究古代语言的学者。

examples.en: The young scholar won a prize for her thesis.
examples.cn: 这位年轻学者因论文获奖。

dict_mnemonic.text: scholar 与 school 同源，学校是学习之地，学者就是长期钻研学问的人。

root: 源自拉丁语 schola（学校、学习），经晚期拉丁语 scholaris 入英语，核心义「长期从事学习与研究的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Scholar means a deep researcher, a student with a scholarship, or a learned person.
sensesIntro.cn: scholar 意为深入研究的学者、获得奖学金的学生，或博学之人。

core.en: A person who gives time to deep study.
core.cn: 把时间投入深入研究的人。

branches.en: The core figure of a specialist researcher.
branches.cn: 专业研究者的核心形象。

branches.en: A student supported by an award.
branches.cn: 获得资助的学生。

branches.en: A person marked by broad learning.
branches.cn: 以广博学识著称的人。

branches.en: Deep research produces a learned reputation.
branches.cn: 深入研究造就博学的声望。

branches.en: Both study seriously, one as a career and one as a student.
branches.cn: 两者都认真治学，一个为职业，一个为学生。

intro.en: Scholar has a family linking learning, schools, and awards.
intro.cn: scholar 有连接学问、学校与奖学金的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin schola, school, is the root of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 schola（学校）是该词族的词根。

items.example: The scholar wrote a long book.
items.exampleCN: 这位学者写了一本厚书。
他没受过多少学校教育。

definition_zh: 无力的；软塌塌的；缺乏生气的；跛行；一瘸一拐地走；跛态
definition_en: lacking firmness or strength; to walk with a halting step; and a halting way of walking
core_image: 生菜叶在手里垂下来，梗再也撑不住叶片
scene: 菜市场收摊前，摊主把一袋放了一天的生菜拎起来，叶片软软地垂向地面。 The lettuce had gone limp in the heat, so she sold it at half price.
sceneCN: 这里是「软塌塌的、失去挺括」（第 1 个义项：物体因失水或疲劳而变软）；句意为生菜在热气里变得软塌塌，她半价卖掉了。图中可辨识物件：塑料袋、垂下的叶片、菜摊的价牌。

pos.zh: 无力的；软塌塌的；缺乏生气的

derivatives.zh: 由 limp 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「无力地；软软地」
由 limp 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「柔软；无力」

senses.title: Soft and lacking firmness
senses.definition: soft and not firm, especially because of heat, tiredness or lack of water
senses.definitionCN: 柔软而不坚挺，尤因受热、疲乏或缺水
senses.example: The lettuce had gone limp in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 生菜在热气里变得软塌塌的。
senses.why: The adjective pictures something that can no longer hold its own weight, so the first sense is physical softness rather than moral weakness.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词的画面是某物再也撑不住自己的重量，所以第一层意思是物理上的软，而不是道德上的弱。

senses.title: Weak and lacking energy
senses.definition: without strength, force or energy, used of a handshake, a performance or a response
senses.definitionCN: 没有力气、力道或精神，用于握手、表现或回应
senses.example: His handshake was limp and brief.
senses.exampleCN: 他的握手无力而短促。
senses.why: A hand that does not grip is physically limp, and from that the word moves to anything that fails to show force.
senses.whyCN: 握手时手不使劲就是物理上的软，由此这个词扩展到任何显不出力道的东西。

senses.title: To walk with a halting step
senses.definition: to walk unevenly because one leg or foot hurts or cannot take full weight
senses.definitionCN: 因一条腿或脚疼痛、吃不住重量而走得高低不平
senses.example: He limped up the stairs with one hand on the rail.
senses.exampleCN: 他一只手扶着栏杆，一瘸一拐地上了楼。
senses.why: The walking verb probably began as a copy of the uneven rhythm itself, which is why the word sounds abrupt and short.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示走路的动词很可能起于对那种一高一低节奏的模仿，所以它读来短促而一顿一顿。

senses.title: A halting way of walking
senses.definition: a way of walking in which one leg moves unevenly, often caused by pain or injury
senses.definitionCN: 一条腿动作不均衡的走路方式，常由疼痛或受伤造成
senses.example: She still walks with a slight limp after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，她走路仍带一点跛态。
senses.why: The noun is the verb turned into a thing: the uneven gait itself becomes something a person has.
senses.whyCN: 名词是动词变成了一件东西：那种一高一低的步态本身，成了一个人身上带着的特征。

intro.en: Limp is a short, blunt word whose origin is uncertain, and it now covers softness, halting movement and the gait itself.
intro.cn: limp 是一个短促的词，来源不确定，如今同时覆盖柔软、跛行与跛态三件事。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the late fourteenth century, and no reliable Latin or Germanic source has been settled; some dictionaries suggest an unrecorded Old English verb of stumbling.
items.cn: 这个动词最早见于十四世纪晚期，可靠的拉丁语或日耳曼语来源尚无定论；一些词典推测它来自一个未被记录的、表示「踉跄」的古英语动词。

items.en: Middle English had limpen and limpien for walking badly, and the short form limp survived.
items.cn: 中古英语有 limpen、limpien 表示走路不稳，后来短形 limp 留存下来。

items.en: The noun a limp appears beside the verb, naming the uneven gait rather than the action of walking.
items.cn: 名词 a limp 与动词同时出现，指那种一高一低的步态，而不是走这个动作。

items.en: The adjective limp, meaning flaccid and unable to hold its shape, is recorded in the eighteenth century, and its link to the verb is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 limp 意为松软、撑不住形状，记录于十八世纪，它与动词的联系并不确定。

items.en: Modern English uses all three parts of speech and extends the adjective to weak handshakes, dull writing and tired vegetables.
items.cn: 现代英语三种词性都在使用，并把形容词扩展到无力的握手、乏味的文字和蔫掉的蔬菜。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers close spellings, including one Latin word that only looks related; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of moving badly or being weak.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词，其中有一个只是形似的拉丁词；近义组收其他表示「走得不稳」或「虚弱」的说法。

entries.definition: In a weak or soft way, without force.
entries.definitionCN: 无力地；软软地。

entries.definition: The quality of being soft or without strength.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软；无力。

entries.definition: Clear and transparent, from Latin limpidus; the spelling is close, but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 清澈透明的，来自拉丁语 limpidus；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Supple and bending easily; only the spelling suggests a link with this word.
entries.definitionCN: 柔韧易弯的；只有拼写暗示它与此词有联系。

entries.definition: To walk with short, awkward steps, often because of pain.
entries.definitionCN: 因疼痛而小步蹒跚地走。

entries.definition: To walk unsteadily as if about to fall.
entries.definitionCN: 摇晃不稳地走，像要摔倒。

entries.definition: To move or speak with hesitation and weakening strength.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或说话犹疑、力道渐弱。

entries.definition: Lacking strength or firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏力气或不够坚挺的。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and imitative, so the hooks come from the hanging leaf, the uneven step and the small family it has gathered.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短促而带有模仿性，所以记忆钩子来自垂下的叶片、一高一低的脚步，以及它聚起的小小词族。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb look identical, so only the sentence tells you whether limp means soft or lame.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词拼写完全相同，只有句子才能告诉你 limp 指「软」还是「跛」。

normal.en: Limp takes -ed and -ing regularly: limped and limping, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: limp 规则地加 -ed、-ing：limped、limping，词尾辅音不双写。

normal.en: Limply and limpness are the adverb and noun built on the adjective with -ly and -ness.
normal.cn: limply 与 limpness 是形容词加 -ly、-ness 构成的副词与名词。

normal.en: Go limp means to lose all tension at once, as a body does when it faints.
normal.cn: go limp 意为一下子失去全部张力，就像人昏过去时身体那样。

normal.en: Limp along means to keep going slowly and with difficulty, like a wounded walker.
normal.cn: limp along 意为像受伤的行人那样，缓慢而吃力地维持下去。

abstract.en: A leaf that cannot hold itself up and a leg that cannot take weight show the same failure of support.
abstract.cn: 撑不住自己的叶子和吃不住重量的腿，显出同一种支撑的失效。

abstract.en: The word refuses to say why: softness and lameness are simply two shapes of not holding firm.
abstract.cn: 这个词不肯说明原因：软与跛，不过都是「撑不住」的两种形状。

abstract.en: A short word with an uncertain past is a good reminder that not every sound can be traced home.
abstract.cn: 一个来历不确定的短词提醒人：并不是每个声音都能被追溯到家。

examples.en: The lettuce had gone limp in the heat.
examples.cn: 生菜在热气里变得软塌塌的。

examples.en: He limped up the stairs with one hand on the rail.
examples.cn: 他一只手扶着栏杆，一瘸一拐地上了楼。

examples.en: She still walks with a slight limp after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后，她走路仍带一点跛态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林普」——林子边一根普普通通的拐杖，撑着人一瘸一拐地走；limp 是跛行。

root: 来源不确定：动词 limp（跛行）最早见于十四世纪晚期，中古英语作 limpen、limpien；形容词 limp（松软）记录于十八世纪，一般认为与动词有某种联系，但没有可靠证据；无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is failing to hold firm; the senses divide into physical softness, lack of force, the halting action, and the gait as a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「撑不住」；义项由此分为物体软塌、力道不足、跛行这个动作，以及作为名词的跛态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lettuce leaf drooping in the hand because its stem can no longer hold it up.
core.cn: 核心意象：生菜叶在手里垂下来，梗再也撑不住叶片。

branches.en: a leaf drooping over the edge of a bag
branches.cn: 垂在袋口的菜叶

branches.en: a hand that does not grip back
branches.cn: 没有回握的手

branches.en: a slow climb with one hand on the rail
branches.cn: 一手扶栏的缓慢上楼

branches.en: a slight unevenness in every step
branches.cn: 每一步里轻微的一高一低

branches.en: one body failing to hold its shape
branches.cn: 一具撑不住形状的身体

intro.cn: 这个词没有前缀，因此条目是它的中古英语来源，以及它在英语中接受的几个后缀。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 洗澡；浸洗；沐浴在
definition_en: to wash yourself or someone in water, or to cover something in light
core_image: 夕阳把整片草地染成金色
scene: 傍晚的风很轻。 The fields were bathed in golden light.
sceneCN: 这里 bathe 是「沐浴在」（第 3 个义项：被光或液体笼罩）；句意是田野沐浴在金黄色的光里。

derivatives.zh: 由 bathe 加 -r 构成，义为「洗浴者；游泳者」
同源名词，义为「洗澡；浴缸」

senses.title: To wash or swim
senses.definition: to wash yourself or another person in water, or to swim in the sea
senses.definitionCN: 在水中洗身或为他人洗身，也指在海里游泳
senses.example: They bathed in the cold river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在冰冷的河里游泳。
senses.why: Bathe is the old verb formed beside the noun bath, and it covers washing and swimming alike.
senses.whyCN: bathe 是与名词 bath 并存的古老动词，既指洗浴也指游泳。

senses.title: To wash a part
senses.definition: to wash a wound or a part of the body gently
senses.definitionCN: 轻柔地清洗伤口或身体某处
senses.example: She bathed the cut with clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 她用清水冲洗伤口。
senses.why: A small part can be bathed just as a whole body can, so the verb covers gentle local washing.
senses.whyCN: 局部也能像全身一样被洗，所以这个动词也指轻柔的局部清洗。

senses.title: To be covered in light
senses.definition: to be covered or filled with light or liquid
senses.definitionCN: 被光或液体笼罩、充满
senses.example: The fields were bathed in golden light.
senses.exampleCN: 田野沐浴在金黄色的光里。
senses.why: Being covered by water became a picture for being covered by light, which gives this figurative sense.
senses.whyCN: 被水覆盖被用作被光覆盖的比喻，于是产生这个引申义。

intro.cn: bathe 是与名词 bath 一同成长起来的古老动词。

items.cn: bathian 意为「在水中洗浴」。

items.en: bathen kept the washing sense.

items.en: bathe covered swimming in the sea.
items.cn: bathe 涵盖在海中游泳。

items.en: bathe in light became a common image.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ba- and -the shape; the near-meaning group gives washing and soaking.

normalIntro.en: Bathe is what you do with water, light or a wound.
normalIntro.cn: bathe 是用水、光或冲洗伤口所做的动作。

normal.en: The past tense is bathed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 bathed。

normal.en: Bathe a wound means wash it gently.

normal.en: Bathe in light means be covered by light.
normal.cn: bathe in light 意为被光笼罩。

normal.en: Bath is the noun and bathe is the verb.

normal.en: The final sound is a soft th.

abstract.en: See a field turning gold at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时田野变成金色。

abstract.en: See a hand rinsing a small cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手冲洗小伤口。

abstract.en: See swimmers in a cold river.
abstract.cn: 想象在冷河里游泳的人。

sensesIntro.en: Washing a body, rinsing a wound and flooding a field with light all use the same water image.
sensesIntro.cn: 洗身、冲伤口与让田野浸在光里，都沿用同一个「水」的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field turning gold at sunset.

definition_zh: 围裙；停机坪；（舞台前缘的）台口
definition_en: a piece of clothing worn over the front of other clothes to keep them clean; also the area where aircraft park at an airport
core_image: 挡在前面的布：一块布挡在身前护住里面的衣服
scene: 妈妈系好围裙开始做饭。 The chef put on an apron before starting to cook in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 apron 是「围裙」（第 1 个义项：护住身前的衣物）；句意为「厨师在下厨前系上了围裙」。该词还可指机场的停机坪或舞台前缘。

pos.zh: 停机坪（机场内飞机停放、装卸的区域）

collocations.phrase: wipe one's hands on the apron

derivatives.zh: apron 加形容词性后缀 -ed 构成，义为「系着围裙的」，多作定语描写人物形象
apron 加否定前缀 un- 与后缀 -ed 构成的少见形容词，义为「未系围裙的」，仅用于描写性语境

senses.title: A garment worn to protect clothes
senses.definition: a piece of cloth tied over the front of the body to keep the clothes underneath clean while cooking or working
senses.definitionCN: 系在身前的布片，做饭或干活时保护里面的衣服不被弄脏
senses.example: Grandma wears a floral apron when she makes dumplings.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶包饺子时系着一条花围裙。
senses.why: The core image is cloth hung in front as a shield; this is the direct, oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是布片挡在身前作屏障；这是该词最直接、最古老的用法。

senses.title: A protective surface or strip resembling an apron
senses.titleCN: 类似围裙的护面或护带
senses.definition: a surface or strip that protects or covers something, shaped like the front protection of an apron
senses.definitionCN: 形似围裙前襟、起保护或覆盖作用的表面或条带
senses.example: The road was rebuilt with a concrete apron at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 道路重修时，入口处铺了混凝土护面。
senses.why: Something spread out in front to protect looks like an apron worn in front of the body.
senses.whyCN: 铺展在前方起保护作用之物，形似穿在身前作保护的围裙。

senses.title: The airport area where aircraft park
senses.definition: the hard-surfaced area of an airport where planes park, load, and are serviced
senses.definitionCN: 机场内飞机停放、装卸与维护的硬化地面区域
senses.example: Ground staff guided the plane to the apron after landing.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机降落后，地勤人员将它引导到停机坪。
senses.why: The paved area spreads out in front of the terminal like a protective apron around the aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 航站楼前的硬化场地铺展延伸，如围裙般环护飞机，故得此名。

senses.title: The front edge of a stage
senses.definition: the part of a stage that extends in front of the curtain toward the audience
senses.definitionCN: 舞台幕布之前、向观众席延伸的部分
senses.example: The actor stepped onto the apron to speak to the audience directly.
senses.exampleCN: 演员走上台口，直接面向观众说话。
senses.why: The stage floor juts forward beyond the main area, apron-like, reaching toward the seats.
senses.whyCN: 台面向主舞台之外前伸，形如围裙的裙摆探向观众席。

intro.en: Apron is a famous case of a word losing an n: it came from napron through misdivision.
intro.cn: apron 是「丢失字母 n」的著名案例：由 napron 经错误切分而来。

items.en: Old French naperon, a diminutive of nape (tablecloth), from Latin mappa (cloth).
items.cn: 古法语 naperon，是 nape（桌布）的小称形式，源自拉丁语 mappa（布）。

items.en: Borrowed into Middle English as napron, meaning a small cloth or protecting cloth.
items.cn: 十四世纪进入中古英语，作 napron，义为小块布或护身之布。

items.en: a napron was misheard and re-cut as an apron, moving the n to the previous word; a napron became an apron.
items.cn: a napron 被误听并重新切分为 an apron，字母 n 移给了前一个冠词，napron 变成了 apron。

items.en: The new form apron established itself in the 1400s and 1500s and became the standard spelling.
items.cn: 新形式 apron 在十五至十六世纪站稳脚跟，成为标准拼写。

items.en: The sense spread from the kitchen garment to protective strips, the airport apron, and the stage apron.
items.cn: 词义从厨房围裙扩展到护面、机场停机坪和舞台台口。

note.en: Watch out for sound-alikes and related protective cloth words.
note.cn: 注意发音相近词及相关防护布类词。

entries.definition: a small cloth for wiping the mouth; shares the French root nape
entries.definitionCN: 餐巾；与 apron 同源于法语 nape（桌布）

entries.definition: table linen, an old word from the same French root
entries.definitionCN: 桌布餐巾类织物；源自同一法语词根的旧词

entries.definition: to try to do something; only the opening letters look similar
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；仅开头拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a loose protective garment, often worn by artists or workers
entries.definitionCN: 罩衫；宽松防护衣，多为画师或工人所穿

entries.definition: protective clothing worn over ordinary clothes, often with sleeves and legs
entries.definitionCN: 工装裤/罩衣；覆盖面比围裙更大的防护服

entries.definition: informal word for the airport parking area, near apron in sense 03
entries.definitionCN: 停机坪（口语说法），与 apron 第 3 义项近义

normalIntro.en: Remember the lost n and the picture of the cloth in front.
normalIntro.cn: 记住那个丢失的 n 和「挡身前的布」的画面。

normal.en: a napron -> an apron: the n jumped from the noun to the article.
normal.cn: a napron → an apron：字母 n 从名词跳到了冠词上。

normal.en: napkin and apron are cousins: both come from nape, the French word for tablecloth.
normal.cn: napkin 与 apron 是亲戚：都来自法语 nape（桌布）。

normal.en: apron strings is a fixed phrase: under one's apron strings means being controlled by someone.
normal.cn: apron strings（围裙带）是固定搭配，under one's apron strings 指「在某人掌控下」。

normal.en: Sound link: 'AY-pron' sounds like 'A-pron' — just the article A plus pron.
normal.cn: 读音联想「诶-普伦」：就像冠词 A 加 pron，好记它的来历。

normal.en: Airport apron: the ground apron-like in front of the terminal where planes park.
normal.cn: 机场停机坪：航站楼前铺展如围裙的地面，飞机停在那里。

abstract.en: Picture a shield made of cloth hanging in front of you.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布做的盾牌挂在身前。

abstract.en: Apron is protection you wear; armor is protection you fight in.
abstract.cn: apron 是穿着的防护，armor 是上阵的铠甲。

abstract.en: One n walked away from napron and never came back.
abstract.cn: 一个字母 n 从 napron 里出走，再也没有回来。

examples.en: She wiped her wet hands on her apron.
examples.cn: 她在围裙上擦了擦湿手。

examples.en: Pilots and ground crews work together on the apron.
examples.cn: 飞行员和地勤人员在停机坪上协同工作。

examples.en: An apron keeps oil stains off your clothes while cooking.
examples.cn: 做饭时围裙能防止油渍弄脏衣服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶铺龙」——诶，围裙一铺开像条小龙挡在身前，油点都溅不到衣服。

root: 源自拉丁语 mappa（布）→ 古法语 nape（桌布）→ naperon（小桌布，护身之布）→ 中古英语 napron → 因误切分 an apron 失去首字母 n。词形演变脉络清晰，misdivision（错误切分）是语言学上著名案例。

sensesIntro.en: From the cloth in front of the body, the word spreads to any apron-like protective area.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「身前的布」出发，词义扩展到一切形似围裙的防护区域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth spread in front as a protective shield
core.cn: 核心意象：铺展在身前、起保护作用的布

branches.en: The kitchen garment that keeps clothes clean.
branches.cn: 护住衣服的厨房围裙。

branches.en: Any protective surface shaped like a front shield.
branches.cn: 一切形似前挡的护面。

branches.en: The airport ground that spreads before the terminal.
branches.cn: 航站楼前铺展的机场停机坪。

branches.en: The stage floor reaching toward the audience.
branches.cn: 伸向观众席的舞台前缘。

branches.cn: 两个义项共享「在前防护」的观念。

intro.en: Apron is a simple noun with few affixes; its story is in sound change, not building blocks.
intro.cn: apron 是个朴素的名词，几乎不用词缀；它的故事在语音演变，而非构词部件。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source mappa also gave the word map.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源 mappa 还派生出 map（地图）一词。

items.example: Mappa is the far source of apron.
items.exampleCN: mappa 是 apron 的远期词源。

items.example: Nape narrowed to mean linen cloth in Old French.
items.exampleCN: nape 在古法语中收窄为餐布之义。

items.example: Napron lost its n through misdivision.
items.exampleCN: napron 因误切分丢掉了首字母 n。

items.example: Napkin keeps the n that apron lost.
items.exampleCN: napkin 保留了 apron 丢失的 n。

items.example: Napery is an old word for household linen.
items.exampleCN: napery 是家用布艺的旧称。

items.example: The aproned cook stirred the soup.
items.exampleCN: 系着围裙的厨师搅动着汤。

latinEntries.example: Mappa mundi once meant a cloth map of the world.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mappa mundi 原指绘在布上的世界地图。

definition_zh: 成熟的；时机成熟的；年纪大的
definition_en: ready to eat or ready to happen
core_image: 枝头熟透的桃子
scene: 果园里的桃子已经成熟，等着人来摘。 The peaches in the orchard were ripe and ready to pick.
sceneCN: 这里 ripe 是「成熟的」（第 1 个义项：果实可以食用）；句意：果园里的桃子已经成熟，等着人来摘。

pos.zh: 成熟的；时机成熟的；年高的

senses.title: Ready to eat
senses.definition: fully grown and ready to eat
senses.definitionCN: 完全长成、可以食用
senses.example: These apples are not ripe yet.
senses.exampleCN: 这些苹果还没熟。
senses.why: Fruit is ripe when it has reached its full season.
senses.whyCN: 果实到了季节的顶点就是熟了。

senses.title: Ready to happen
senses.definition: fully prepared for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为某事的发生做好充分准备
senses.example: The country was ripe for change.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家变革的时机已成熟。
senses.why: A ready time is like fruit ready to fall.
senses.whyCN: 时机成熟就像果实准备落地。

senses.title: Advanced in years
senses.definition: old and full of experience
senses.definitionCN: 年事已高且阅历丰富
senses.example: She lived to a ripe old age.
senses.exampleCN: 她活到了高龄。
senses.why: A long life is also a kind of ripening.
senses.whyCN: 漫长的一生也是一种成熟。

intro.en: Ripe comes from Old English rīpe, ready for harvest.
intro.cn: ripe 源自古英语 rīpe，意为可以收获的。

items.en: Ripe means ready for harvest.
items.cn: ripe 意为可以收获。

items.en: The word spreads from fruit to plans.
items.cn: 这个词从果实扩展到计划。

items.en: Ripe for change means ready for it.
items.cn: ripe for change 意为准备好改变。

items.en: Ripe old age praises long life.
items.cn: ripe old age 赞颂长寿。

items.en: Ripen grows as the verb.
items.cn: ripen 成为对应的动词。

note.en: Ripe fruit is ready to eat; mature is the more general word.

normal.en: Ripe fruit falls easily from the branch.

normal.en: Ripe bananas are soft and sweet.

normal.en: The time is ripe means now is the moment.

normal.en: Ripe for change means ready for it.

branches.en: Good timing and long life both mean fullness.
branches.cn: 好时机与长寿都意味着圆满。

definition_zh: 在头顶上方；头顶上的；经常开支；过顶球
definition_en: above a person's head, fixed or passing high above the ground, or the regular costs a business pays just to keep running
core_image: 老街上方电车线拉成一张网，遮阳布把摊位压在下面
scene: 夏天的老街上，电车线在头顶拉成一张网，卖冰的小贩把遮阳布支得更低。 A plane passed overhead, drowning out the conversation on the pavement.
sceneCN: 这里 overhead 是「在头顶上方」（第 1 个义项：副词，位置在头顶之上）；句意为一架飞机从头顶飞过，盖住了人行道上的谈话，画面是老街上方的电车线网。

pos.zh: 经常开支；间接费用；过顶球

derivatives.zh: overhead 加复数词尾 -s 后固化为名词，专指企业的经常开支
由 overhead 与 projector 复合而成，义为「高架投影仪」
由 overhead 与 line 复合而成，义为「架空线路」，供车辆取电

senses.title: Above a person's head
senses.titleCN: 在头顶上方；在空中（副词）
senses.definition: in the air directly above someone, without touching the ground or any surface
senses.definitionCN: 在空中正对某人头顶的位置，不接触地面或任何表面
senses.example: A fan hummed overhead while we waited in the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在走廊里等着，头顶上一台风扇嗡嗡地转。
senses.why: The compound is over plus head, so the first sense simply puts a thing on the far side of the head; no metaphor is involved yet.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词就是 over 加 head，所以第一个义项只是把东西放到头顶的另一侧；此时还没有任何比喻。

senses.title: Fixed or passing above the ground
senses.titleCN: 头顶上的；架空的（形容词）
senses.definition: placed high enough to clear people and traffic, as wires, railways or beams
senses.definitionCN: 架得足够高，能让开行人与车辆，如电线、铁路或横梁
senses.example: The village still gets its power from overhead cables.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子仍靠架空电缆供电。
senses.why: Once the word marks the space above the head, anything built to occupy that space takes the same label, so the adverb becomes an adjective describing structures.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出头顶那片空间，任何被造来占用那片空间的东西都能带上它，于是副词变形容词，用来形容构筑物。

senses.title: The regular costs of running a business
senses.definition: the fixed costs of running a business, such as rent, lighting and administration, that are not tied to one product
senses.definitionCN: 企业运转的固定成本，如房租、照明与行政开支，不直接计入某一件产品
senses.example: The company cut its overheads by moving to a smaller office.
senses.exampleCN: 公司搬到更小的办公室，压低了经常开支。
senses.why: In bookkeeping these costs sit above the individual jobs the way a ceiling sits above a room: they must be paid whatever is produced, so the word for what is above the head becomes the word for costs that hang over the whole business.
senses.whyCN: 在账目里，这些成本像天花板一样悬在每一项具体工作之上：不管生产什么都得付，于是「头顶之上」的词变成了悬在整个生意上方的开销。

senses.title: A stroke hit down from above
senses.definition: in tennis, squash or badminton, a stroke played with the racket raised above the head and swung downwards
senses.definitionCN: 网球、壁球或羽毛球中，把球拍举过头顶向下击出的球
senses.example: He finished the point with a powerful overhead smash.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记有力的过顶扣杀拿下这一分。
senses.why: The sporting sense keeps the physical picture without any transfer: the racket really does travel above the head, so the same word names the shot by the place it is played.
senses.whyCN: 运动义没有转移，只是照搬了身体画面：球拍确实从头顶上方挥过，于是同一个词按击球的位置给这一拍命名。

intro.en: Overhead is an English compound of two inherited words, first a phrase for position and later a label for wires, railways and business costs.
intro.cn: overhead 是由两个英语固有词构成的复合词，先是表示位置的短语，后来用来标注电线、铁路与经营成本。

items.en: Over and head both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, so the compound was put together inside English's own vocabulary.
items.cn: over 与 head 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，所以这个复合词是在英语自身词汇里拼合的。

items.en: Old English wrote ofer heafod as two words for something passing above a person's head.
items.cn: 古英语把 ofer heafod 写成两个词，指从头顶上方经过的东西。

items.en: Middle English kept the phrase for position and began to apply it to beams and roofs lying above a room.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个表示位置的短语，并开始用它指横在房间上方的梁与顶。

items.en: Railways and telegraph wires made an adjective useful, and businesses began to speak of overhead as the cost of simply keeping the doors open.
items.cn: 铁路与电报线让形容词用法有了用处，商家开始用 overhead 指仅仅维持开门营业所需的花费。

items.en: Modern English uses the adverb for position, the plural nouns for fixed costs, and a singular noun for a stroke struck downwards.
items.cn: 现代英语用副词表示位置，用复数名词表示固定开支，又用单数名词指自上而下击出的球。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plural noun and the compounds built with this word; the near-meaning group gathers words of position above and words for business costs.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复数名词以及由它构成的复合词；近义组收表示「上方位置」与表示「经营成本」的词。

entries.definition: The plural noun for the fixed costs of running a business.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业经营固定成本的复数名词。

entries.definition: A device that throws an image onto a screen from a lit sheet below.
entries.definitionCN: 把下方灯箱上的图像投到幕布上的设备。

entries.definition: A wire carried above a road or track to supply electric power.
entries.definitionCN: 架在道路或轨道上方、用于供电的电线。

entries.definition: A railway built on a raised structure above street level.
entries.definitionCN: 建在街面以上高架结构上的铁路。

entries.definition: In a higher position than something else, often directly over it.
entries.definitionCN: 位置高于某物，常指正上方。

entries.definition: High up in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 在空中高处。

entries.definition: Money spent in doing something, especially for a business.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事花掉的钱，尤指企业开支。

entries.definition: The amounts of money that must be paid to run or produce something.
entries.definitionCN: 为运转或生产某物必须支付的金额。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply over plus head, and its hooks return to that height, to the structures that occupy it, and to the costs that hang over a business.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 over 加 head，记忆钩子都回到那个高度、占用那个高度的构筑物，以及悬在生意上方的成本。

normal.en: Overhead is over plus head, so anything placed or moving above the head can take the word.
normal.cn: overhead 是 over 加 head，凡是放在头顶上方或从头顶移过的东西都能用它。

normal.en: The adverb came first and the adjective followed, which is why wires and railways are described with the same word.
normal.cn: 先有副词，后有形容词，所以电线与铁路也用同一个词来形容。

normal.en: Overheads are called that because the rent and the lighting hang over every job like a ceiling.
normal.cn: 经常开支得名，是因为房租与照明像天花板一样悬在每一项工作之上。

normal.en: The final s matters: overheads in the plural is the business sense, while an overhead in sport is one stroke.
normal.cn: 末尾的 s 很关键：复数 overheads 是经营开支，运动里的 an overhead 则是一记球。

normal.en: An overhead smash keeps the literal picture, since the racket really passes above the head.
normal.cn: 过顶扣杀保留了字面画面，因为球拍确实从头顶上方挥过。

abstract.en: A tram wire drawn across a summer street is the word as pure position.
abstract.cn: 夏天街道上方拉过的一条电车线，就是这个词作为纯粹位置的样子。

abstract.en: A ceiling with lamps hanging from it turns height into a bill somebody has to pay.
abstract.cn: 挂着灯的天花板，把高度变成了一张总得有人付的账单。

abstract.en: A raised arm coming down on a ball shows the same word at the moment it becomes an action.
abstract.cn: 高举的手臂向下击球，显示同一个词变成动作的那一瞬。

examples.en: A fan hummed overhead while we waited in the corridor.
examples.cn: 我们在走廊里等着，头顶上一台风扇嗡嗡地转。

examples.en: The company cut its overheads by moving to a smaller office.
examples.cn: 公司搬到更小的办公室，压低了经常开支。

examples.en: He finished the point with a powerful overhead smash.
examples.cn: 他用一记有力的过顶扣杀拿下这一分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃海德」——欧沃把账单举过头顶，抬头一看，全是开销。

root: overhead 由古英语 ofer（在上）与 heafod（头）合成，字面即「在头顶之上」；两半都属日耳曼语固有词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the space above the head; the senses move from position, to structures that occupy it, to costs that hang over a business, and to a stroke struck from above.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是头顶上方那片空间；义项从位置，转到占用这片空间的构筑物，再转到悬在生意上方的成本，最后转到自上而下的击球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tram wires crossing above an old street while a vendor pulls his awning lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：老街上方电车线交错，小贩把遮阳布压得更低。

branches.en: a fan turning above people in a corridor
branches.cn: 走廊里在人们头顶转的风扇

branches.en: wires strung high across a village street
branches.cn: 高高拉过村街的电线

branches.en: a rent bill that arrives whatever is sold
branches.cn: 不管卖不卖货都要来的房租单

branches.en: a racket raised and swung down at a ball
branches.cn: 高举后向下击球的球拍

branches.en: one height, once built of wire and once built of money
branches.cn: 同一种高度，一次由电线搭成，一次由钱搭成

intro.en: The word puts the Old English word for over in front of the word for head, and the same pattern then feeds compounds and a plural noun.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在上」的词放在表示「头」的词前面，同一模式又生出复合词与一个复数名词。

latinIntro.en: This is a native Germanic compound with no Latin family; Latin super is a distant Indo-European relative of over, not a source of this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语固有的复合词，没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 super 只是 over 的印欧远亲，并非这个词的来源。

definition_zh: 洞察力；洞见；深刻的理解
definition_en: a clear and deep understanding of a person, problem, or situation
core_image: 一束光照进原本昏暗的屋子，屋里摆着的东西忽然看清楚了
scene: 会议开到深夜，白板上写满了没人看得懂的关系图。 Her insight into the market saved the company from a costly mistake.
sceneCN: 这里 insight 是「洞察、深刻的理解」（第 1 个义项：对人或问题清楚深刻的理解），句意是她对市场的洞察让公司免于一次代价高昂的错误。画面里能看到的物件：白板、关系图、台灯。

pos.zh: 名词：洞察力；洞见；深刻理解

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ful 构成，义为「富有洞见的」
由 insightful 加 -ly 构成，义为「有洞见地」
由 insightful 加 -ness 构成，义为「洞察力」

senses.title: Deep understanding
senses.definition: the ability to see the true nature of a situation or a person, often hidden from others
senses.definitionCN: 看清情境或人物真实本质的能力，这种本质常为他人所不见
senses.example: The book gives a rare insight into village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对乡村生活给出了罕见的洞见。
senses.why: In- plus sight: sight turned inwards, past the surface, to what is really there.
senses.whyCN: in- 加 sight：向里看的目光，越过表面，看到真正存在的东西。

senses.title: A sudden clear idea
senses.definition: a sudden clear understanding that solves a problem or changes how you see it
senses.definitionCN: 突然获得的清晰理解，解决了问题或改变了看法
senses.example: She had an insight while walking home and rewrote the whole plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她走回家的路上顿悟，把整个计划重写了。
senses.why: Turning sight inwards can happen in a flash; the word also names that flash rather than the lasting ability.
senses.whyCN: 「向里看」可以发生在一瞬之间，这个词也指那一瞬，而不只是持久的能力。

senses.title: Information that reveals something
senses.definition: useful knowledge about how something really works, gained from inside
senses.definitionCN: 从内部获得的、关于某事物真实运作方式的有用知识
senses.example: Analysts used buying data to gain insight into customer habits.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师用购买数据来了解顾客习惯。
senses.why: Business and research adopted the word for knowledge that comes from looking inside the data.
senses.whyCN: 商业与研究领域用这个词指从数据内部看出来的知识。

intro.en: Insight is a native compound of in and sight, formed on the model of the verb to see into.
intro.cn: insight 是本族语复合词，由 in 与 sight 组成，按「看进去」的说法造成。

items.en: Sith "sight, view" is Old English, related to the verb to see.
items.cn: sith「视觉、景象」见于古英语，与动词 see 有关。

items.en: The preposition in was freely combined with nouns to mark the inner side.
items.cn: 古英语介词 in 常与名词组合，表示内侧。

items.en: The noun insight appears in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries in the sense of inner vision.
items.cn: 名词 insight 在十三、十四世纪出现，义为「内心的看见」。

items.en: The sense shifts from vision to understanding during the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪，词义从「视觉」转向「理解」。

items.en: Modern psychology and management made insight a technical term for self-knowledge and analysis.
items.cn: 现代心理学与管理学把 insight 变成自我认识与分析的术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sight image; the near-meaning group holds other words for understanding.
note.cn: 形近组共享「看见」这一意象；近义组收其他表示「理解」的词。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or something seen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视力、景象」，是复合的另一半。

entries.definition: The ability to see what is coming; built with fore- instead of in-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「远见」，用 fore- 而非 in- 构成。

entries.definition: Understanding of events only after they happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事后聪明」，用 hind-「后面」构成。

entries.definition: The general word for knowing how something works.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理解」，是最宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: The way something is noticed or interpreted, not necessarily deep.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知觉、看法」，不一定深刻。

entries.definition: Knowledge felt without proof, often unspoken.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直觉」，指没有证据的感觉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks play on the literal "sight turned inwards" and the phrases the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用字面的「向里看的目光」，以及这个词的常用搭配。

normal.en: in plus sight: seeing inside, not just seeing.
normal.cn: in 加 sight：看见里面，而不只是看见。

normal.en: Compare foresight and hindsight, built the same way.
normal.cn: 可对比用同样方式构成的 foresight 与 hindsight。

normal.en: Gain insight into a problem before proposing a fix.
normal.cn: 在提出解决办法前先深入了解问题。

normal.en: A good interview yields insight, not just quotes.
normal.cn: 好的访谈带来洞察，而不只是引语。

normal.en: Insightful writing shows rather than tells.
normal.cn: 有洞见的文字靠展示，而不是靠陈述。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp switched on inside a dark shed.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗的棚屋里忽然亮起一盏灯。

abstract.en: Insight is seeing the wiring behind the wall.
abstract.cn: 洞察是看见墙背后的线路。

abstract.en: Insight arrives without knocking, usually in the middle of something else.
abstract.cn: 洞察从不敲门，常在别的事情中间到来。

examples.en: The interviews gave us insight into how parents choose schools.
examples.cn: 这些访谈让我们深入了解家长如何择校。

examples.en: He has real insight into his own mistakes.
examples.cn: 他对自己的错误有真正的洞察。

examples.en: The poem ends with a quiet insight about grief.
examples.cn: 这首诗以对悲伤的平静领悟收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 sight」——因为看得见里面，才有洞见

root: 英语本族语复合词：古英语 in「在内」+ siht/sith「视觉、景象」（与 see 同源）。按「看进内部」的说法造成，十七世纪词义由「内在视象」转为「深刻理解」，与 foresight、hindsight 同构。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: lasting deep understanding, the sudden flash, and useful inside knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：持久的深刻理解、突然的顿悟，以及有用的内部知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp switches on inside a dark shed and everything becomes clear.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗棚屋里亮起一盏灯，一切忽然清楚。

branches.en: THE LAMP: the lasting ability to see deeply.
branches.cn: 台灯这条线：持久地看得深的能力。

branches.en: THE FLASH: understanding that arrives in a moment.
branches.cn: 闪光这条线：一瞬间到来的理解。

branches.en: THE DATA: knowledge gained from inside a system.
branches.cn: 数据这条线：从系统内部获得的知识。

branches.en: THE LINK: both come from looking inward rather than at surfaces.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都来自朝里看而非看表面。

branches.en: THE TONE: the sudden sense is more personal and emotional.
branches.cn: 语气线：顿悟义更个人化、更有情绪。

intro.en: Insight is in- plus the native noun sight, exactly parallel to foresight and hindsight.
intro.cn: insight 是 in- 加本族名词 sight，与 foresight、hindsight 完全同构。

latinIntro.en: The word is not Latin; the Latin-derived noun sight of the mind is listed only as a comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词并非拉丁来源，列出的拉丁同源对照词仅供参考。

items.example: It marks the direction of looking.

items.meaning: the power or act of seeing
items.example: The second half supplies the image.
