用 hind- 的同一模式。

items.example: Over- shifts the sense to missing something.
Also names what is looked at.

items.meaning: the ability to see or imagine
items.exampleCN: 与 sight 对应的拉丁来源词。

definition_zh: 重要地；重要的是；更为重要的是
definition_en: in a way that matters, used especially at the start of a statement to mark the point that deserves most attention
core_image: 一长串话讲完后，说话人抬起手指，把最后一句又说了一遍
scene: 会议上发言人讲完一堆数据，忽然抬起手，把最后一句又重复一遍。 Importantly, no one lost money in the end.
sceneCN: 这里 importantly 是「重要的是」（第 1 个义项：用来标出最该听的那一点），句意是重要的是，最后没有人亏钱。画面里有会议室、一叠数据纸和一只抬起的手。

pos.zh: 副词：重要地；重要的是（用于强调某一点）

senses.title: Marking the key point
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a clause to single out the point that matters most
senses.definitionCN: 置于分句开头，挑出最该被听见的那一点
senses.example: Importantly, the medicine has no serious side effects.
senses.exampleCN: 重要的是，这种药没有严重的副作用。
senses.why: Here the adverb acts like a spotlight rather than describing how an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 此时副词像一束追光，而非描述动作怎么做的。

senses.title: Adding a weightier point
senses.titleCN: 更重要的是（追加更重的理由）
senses.definition: used with more or most to add a point that outweighs earlier ones
senses.definitionCN: 与 more、most 连用，补充一条压过前文的分量更重的理由
senses.example: The trip was cheap and, more importantly, safe.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行很便宜，更重要的是安全。
senses.why: The adverb now ranks reasons, telling the listener which one should be kept.
senses.whyCN: 此时副词在给理由排位次，告诉听者该记住哪一条。

senses.title: In a weighty manner
senses.definition: in a manner that suggests the speaker or doer takes themselves seriously
senses.definitionCN: 以一种自视甚重的神态行事
senses.example: He cleared his throat importantly before beginning.
senses.exampleCN: 他煞有介事地清了清嗓子才开始。
senses.why: The old literal sense survives here: the adverb describes how something is done, not what is ranked.
senses.whyCN: 此处保留的是较早的字面义：副词描述做法神态，而不是给内容排位次。

intro.en: Importantly is the adverb of important, built on a Latin verb for carrying things in.
intro.cn: importantly 是 important 的副词，底子是拉丁语中「搬进来」的动词。

items.en: Importare combined in, into, and portare, to carry, giving the sense of bringing something in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 把 in「进入」与 portare「搬运」合起来，表示把东西搬进来。

items.en: The verb extended to meanings that carry weight, so to import came to mean to signify.
items.cn: 这个动词引申到「承载分量」的事上，to import 因而有了「意味着」的意思。

items.en: French formed important, and the -ment adverb that went with it.
items.cn: 法语造出 important，也造出了与它相配的 -ment 副词。

items.en: English made the adverb on its own pattern, adding -ly to important in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语按自己的构词方式，在十七世纪给 important 加上 -ly 做出副词。

items.en: The sentence-opening use, as in more importantly, spread in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 置于句首的用法，如 more importantly，到二十世纪才广泛流行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family; the near-meaning group gathers other spotlight adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组收 import 一族词；近义组收其他起「打光」作用的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective that stands before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，放在名词前。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指「重要性」。

entries.definition: With irritation at having to wait; a near neighbour in spelling only.
entries.definitionCN: 「不耐烦地」，与 importantly 拼写相近，意思无关。

entries.definition: Used to point out a fact worth noticing.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「尤其是、值得注意的是」。

entries.definition: Used to mark the point on which the outcome turns.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「关键是」，标出决定成败的那一点。

entries.definition: To a degree large enough to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「显著地」，指程度大到产生影响。

normalIntro.en: The hooks focus on the two live patterns: sentence-opening spotlight and the more importantly ranking.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子集中在两个活跃用法上：句首打光，以及 more importantly 的排位。

normal.en: Take important, add -ly, and put it at the front: the adverb becomes a spotlight.
normal.cn: important 加 -ly 放到句首，这个副词就变成一束追光。

normal.en: More importantly is a ranking signal: whatever follows beats whatever came before.
normal.cn: more importantly 是排位信号：后面的理由压过前面的。

normal.en: Most importantly is the last shot in a list, the one you want the reader to keep.
normal.cn: most importantly 是一串内容里的最后一枪，是希望读者记住的那一条。

normal.en: Equally importantly means the second reason weighs as much as the first.
normal.cn: equally importantly 表示第二条理由与第一条一样重。

normal.en: When it describes a manner rather than ranking, it sounds old-fashioned and slightly comic.
normal.cn: 当它描述神态而非排位时，听起来有点古旧，还带点滑稽。

abstract.en: Spotlight adverbs are a grammar of attention: they tell a listener where to spend memory.
abstract.cn: 这类打光副词是一套注意力语法，告诉听者该把记忆花在哪。

abstract.en: The word carries its history openly: it borrowed the weight of goods and now spends it on arguments.
abstract.cn: 这个词把历史明明白白地带着：它借来货物的重量，如今花在论证上。

abstract.en: Used too often, it loses its light, since everything cannot be the most important thing.
abstract.cn: 用得太频繁，它就会失去光亮，因为不可能每件事都最重要。

examples.en: Importantly, the new bus route reaches the hospital.
examples.cn: 重要的是，新公交线路通到医院。

examples.en: The plan is cheap and, more importantly, quick to carry out.
examples.cn: 这个方案花钱少，更重要的是执行得快。

examples.en: She nodded importantly and then said nothing at all.
examples.cn: 她煞有介事地点了点头，然后一个字也没说。

dict_mnemonic.text: important 重要的 + -ly 副词词尾——以「重要」的方式说出来，就是「重要的是」

root: 由 important 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；important 出自拉丁语 importare「搬进来」（in + portare「搬运」）经法语传入英语。句首强调用法在二十世纪广泛流行。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a spotlight at the start of a point, a ranking signal with more or most, and an old literal manner sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：句首点出重点，与 more、most 连用排位次，以及较古的「神态郑重」字面用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised finger repeating the last sentence because that is the one to keep.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抬起的手把最后一句话再说一遍，因为那才是要记住的。

branches.en: THE SPOTLIGHT: at the start of a clause it names the point that matters.
branches.cn: 追光线：置于分句开头时，它点出真正要紧的那一点。

branches.en: THE RANK: with more and most it orders reasons by weight.
branches.cn: 排位线：与 more、most 连用时，它按分量给理由排序。

branches.en: THE MANNER: describing a pompous way of acting keeps the old literal sense.
branches.cn: 神态线：形容做作的举止，保留的是较早的字面义。

branches.en: THE WRITING: in reports it marks what a reader should carry away.
branches.cn: 写作线：在报告里，它标出读者该带走的那句话。

branches.en: THE WARNING: overuse empties it, since every sentence cannot be the key one.
branches.cn: 警示线：滥用会掏空它，因为不可能每句都是关键句。

intro.en: The table shows how -ly turns adjectives into sentence adverbs and how the family hangs together.
intro.cn: 此表展示 -ly 如何把形容词变成句子副词，以及这一族词如何挂在一起。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin importare, from in and portare.
latinIntro.cn: 底子是拉丁语 importare，由 in 与 portare 组成。

items.meaning: in a way that marks what matters
items.example: Importantly, the door was left open.
items.exampleCN: 重要的是，那扇门一直开着。

items.example: An important letter arrived this morning.
items.exampleCN: 今天早上来了一封重要的信。

items.example: The importance of the find was clear at once.
items.exampleCN: 这一发现的重要性一眼就看得出来。

items.example: He was late and, more importantly, unprepared.
items.exampleCN: 他迟到了，更重要的是毫无准备。

items.meaning: to the same degree, a partner in the phrase equally importantly
items.meaningCN: 副词：同样地，可与 importantly 组成固定说法
items.example: The two rooms are equally warm.

items.meaningCN: 副词：尤其是、值得注意的是
items.example: Several guests, notably her aunt, arrived early.
items.exampleCN: 几位客人到得早，尤其是她姑妈。

items.example: They import steel for the yard.

items.meaningCN: 短语：说来也巧，也由同一副词构成
items.example: Importantly enough, the key was still in the lock.
items.exampleCN: 说来也巧，钥匙还插在锁上。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语分词：带有分量或意义的

definition_zh: 暴乱；骚乱；极其好笑的人或事；参与暴乱
definition_en: a violent public disturbance, or something very funny
core_image: 深夜广场上混乱的人群
scene: 广场上的骚乱直到深夜才慢慢平息。 The riot in the square only calmed down late at night.
sceneCN: 这里 riot 是「骚乱」（第 1 个义项：公众场所的暴力混乱）；句意：广场上的骚乱直到深夜才慢慢平息。

pos.zh: 暴乱；骚乱；极好笑的人或事

senses.title: A violent crowd
senses.definition: a violent disturbance by a crowd in public
senses.definitionCN: 人群在公共场所的暴力骚乱
senses.example: The riot broke out after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
senses.why: A crowd that loses control becomes a riot.
senses.whyCN: 失去控制的人群就成了骚乱。

senses.title: Very funny
senses.definition: a person or thing that is very funny
senses.definitionCN: 非常滑稽的人或事
senses.example: His story was an absolute riot.
senses.exampleCN: 他的故事实在太逗了。
senses.why: Wild laughter feels like a small riot.
senses.whyCN: 狂笑的感觉就像一场小小的骚动。

senses.title: To join a riot
senses.definition: to take part in a violent public disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 参与公众场所的暴力骚乱
senses.example: Crowds rioted outside the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在旧工厂外暴动。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为行为本身。

intro.en: Riot comes from Old French riote, a quarrel or wild behaviour.
intro.cn: riot 源自古法语 riote，意为争吵或放荡行为。

items.en: Riote means a quarrel.
items.cn: riote 意为争吵。

items.en: The word also suggests wild living.
items.cn: 该词也暗示放荡的生活。

items.en: Riot comes to mean public disorder.
items.cn: riot 逐渐指公众骚乱。

items.en: Riot police appear to control crowds.
items.cn: 防暴警察出现以控制人群。

items.en: A riot can also mean great fun.
items.cn: a riot 也可以指极大的乐趣。

note.en: A riot is violent; a protest may be peaceful.
note.cn: riot 是暴力的，protest 可能是和平的。

entries.definition: a person who riots
entries.definitionCN: 暴乱者

entries.definition: wild and noisy
entries.definitionCN: 暴乱的；喧闹的

entries.definition: to decay
entries.definitionCN: 腐烂

entries.definition: a lack of order
entries.definitionCN: 混乱

entries.definition: a public show of disagreement
entries.definitionCN: 抗议

entries.definition: an act that breaks the peace
entries.definitionCN: 骚动

normalIntro.en: A riot is a crowd that has lost its brakes.
normalIntro.cn: riot 就是失去刹车的人群。

normal.en: Riot police deal with violent crowds.
normal.cn: riot police 应对暴力人群。

normal.en: To start a riot is to cause disorder.
normal.cn: start a riot 就是引发混乱。

normal.en: Run riot means act without control.
normal.cn: run riot 意为失控妄为。

normal.en: A riot of colour means many bright colours.
normal.cn: a riot of colour 意为五彩缤纷。

normal.en: If a show is a riot, it is very funny.
normal.cn: 如果演出是 a riot，就说明它非常逗。

abstract.en: Picture a street full of shouting shadows.
abstract.cn: 想象满是呼喊人影的街道。

abstract.en: Imagine laughter breaking out like a small storm.
abstract.cn: 想象笑声像小风暴一样爆发。

abstract.en: Think of a garden bursting with wild colour.
abstract.cn: 想象花园里色彩狂放。

examples.en: The riot lasted until dawn.
examples.cn: 骚乱持续到黎明。

examples.en: The party was a riot from start to finish.
examples.cn: 这场聚会从头到尾都非常欢乐。

examples.en: The crowd rioted after the decision.
examples.cn: 裁决之后人群发生了暴动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「riot」听起来像「乱特」——特别乱的场面，就是骚乱。

root: 古法语 riote（争吵、放荡）→ 公众骚乱 → 动词「参与暴乱」，核心义「失控的喧嚣」。

sensesIntro.en: A riot is a violent public disturbance, a very funny thing, or the act of rioting.
sensesIntro.cn: riot 指暴力骚乱、极好笑的事物，或参与暴乱的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with no brakes.
core.cn: 核心意象：失去刹车的人群。

branches.en: A violent crowd is the public sense.
branches.cn: 暴力人群是公众义。

branches.en: Uncontrolled laughter borrows the wild image.
branches.cn: 失控的笑借用了狂放的意象。

branches.en: The verb names joining the disorder.
branches.cn: 动词义指加入混乱。

branches.en: The noun and verb both point at the same streets.
branches.cn: 名词与动词都指向同样的街头。

branches.en: Violence and wild fun both mean losing control.
branches.cn: 暴力与狂乐都意味着失去控制。

intro.en: Riot is a French borrowing with no living prefix.
intro.cn: riot 是法语借词，没有仍在使用的词缀。

latinIntro.en: French riote is its direct parent.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 riote 是它的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: riot 去掉了词尾的 e。
这个复合词指一支警力。

items.example: Run riot uses the wild idea.
items.exampleCN: run riot 使用了狂放的意象。

definition_zh: 消失；突然不见；使（某物）消失；灭绝、不复存在
definition_en: to disappear suddenly and completely
core_image: 一只兔子被人一晃，转眼连影子都不见了
scene: 魔术师掀开黑色幕布，台上那只鸟扑扇了两下就不见了。 The coin vanished from his hand before we could blink.
sceneCN: 这里 vanish 是「消失、突然不见」（第 1 个义项：突然且彻底地不见）；句意为那枚硬币在我们眨眼之前就从他手里消失了。鸟连影子都没留下，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：消失、突然不见；使消失；灭绝、不复存在

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「消失的、正在逐渐消失的」，如 vanishing point
形容词，义为「已消失的、不复存在的」
名词，义为「虚荣、空虚」，与 vanish 同源于拉丁语 vanus「空的」
形容词，义为「迅速消逝的」，同源且更书面
名词短语，义为「消失点、尽头」

senses.title: To disappear suddenly
senses.definition: to disappear suddenly and completely from sight
senses.definitionCN: 突然且彻底地从视野中消失
senses.example: The coin vanished from his hand before we could blink.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚硬币在我们眨眼之前就从他手里消失了。
senses.why: Latin vanus means empty; what vanishes leaves empty space where it stood.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vanus 意为「空的」；消失之物站过的地方就空了下来。

senses.title: To disappear by magic
senses.titleCN: 被变没了：靠手法让东西不见
senses.definition: to make something disappear as if by magic, or to disappear that way
senses.definitionCN: 像变戏法一样使某物消失，或那样消失
senses.example: The magician made the silk scarf vanish in a flash.
senses.exampleCN: 魔术师一下子让那条丝巾消失不见了。
senses.why: Magic borrows the word for the most literal emptiness: the object is gone and the hand is shown empty.
senses.whyCN: 魔术借这个词表达最字面的「空」：物件没了，手心也摊开是空的。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.titleCN: 不存在了：彻底消失、灭绝
senses.definition: to cease to exist, often gradually and on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 不再存在，常指逐渐、大范围地消失
senses.example: Many small languages may vanish within this century.
senses.exampleCN: 许多小语种可能在本世纪内消失。
senses.why: The empty place is no longer a spot on stage but a whole category that is gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个空位不再只是舞台上的一块地方，而是一整个类别不复存在。

senses.title: To fade from use
senses.titleCN: 淡出使用：渐渐从日常里退场
senses.definition: to disappear from common use or from memory
senses.definitionCN: 从常用范围或记忆中淡出
senses.example: The old custom has almost vanished from the countryside.
senses.exampleCN: 这项旧风俗在乡间已几乎消失。
senses.why: Nothing dramatic is needed; the word covers quiet absence as well as sudden loss.
senses.whyCN: 不必有戏剧性场面；这个词既指突然丢失，也指安静的缺席。

senses.title: To become zero
senses.definition: to drop suddenly to nothing, said of amounts or chances
senses.definitionCN: 指数量或机会突然降到零
senses.example: All our savings vanished in one bad deal.
senses.exampleCN: 所有积蓄在一次糟糕的交易中化为乌有。
senses.why: A number that disappears leaves the same empty place as an object that disappears.
senses.whyCN: 一个消失的数字留下的空位，和消失的物件完全相同。

intro.en: Vanish goes back to Latin vanus, empty, through the verb evanescere, to pass away.
intro.cn: vanish 上溯到拉丁语 vanus「空的」，经由动词 evanescere「逝去」而来。

items.en: The adjective vanus meant empty, hollow or without substance.
items.cn: 形容词 vanus 意为空的、虚的、没有实质的。

items.en: The verb evanescere meant to pass away or fade from sight, built with the prefix e- meaning out.
items.cn: 动词 evanescere 意为逝去、从视野中淡出，由表示向外的前缀 e- 构成。

items.en: Old French esvanir shortened the word and kept the sense of disappearing completely.
items.cn: 古法语 esvanir 缩短了这个词，保留了彻底消失的意思。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, spelling it variously before settling on vanish.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，拼法几经变化才定成 vanish。

items.en: Modern English extended it from objects disappearing to languages, customs and sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语把它从物件消失扩展到语言、风俗与金钱。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of emptiness; the near-meaning group holds verbs of going out of sight.
note.cn: 形近组沿表达「空」的拉丁词干；近义组收表示离开视野的动词。

entries.definition: Emptiness turned into pride; same Latin vanus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「虚荣」，同出拉丁 vanus「空的」。

entries.definition: Fading quickly away, closer to the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迅速消逝的」，更接近拉丁动词形式。

entries.definition: The act of disappearing; used in vanishing point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「消失（的）」，见于 vanishing point。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the state of being gone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，罕用，义为「消失的状态」。

entries.definition: The plain word for going out of sight, without the suddenness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不见了」，最普通的说法，不带突兀感。

entries.definition: To grow weaker and less visible by degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「渐渐褪去」，一点一点变淡。

entries.definition: To turn into vapour, or to melt away like vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「蒸发」，像汽一样散去。

entries.definition: To break up and pass into nothing or into a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「溶解、消散」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the empty-space core and phrases such as vanish into thin air.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「空出位置」的核心意象与 vanish into thin air 这类搭配。

normal.en: Vanish shares a root with vanity: both come from a Latin word for empty.
normal.cn: vanish 与 vanity 同根，都出自拉丁语「空的」。

normal.en: Vanish into thin air is the phrase for a disappearance with no explanation.
normal.cn: vanish into thin air 指毫无解释地不见。

normal.en: A magician makes things vanish, but the hand is simply faster than the eye.
normal.cn: 魔术师让东西消失，其实只是手比眼快。

normal.en: Languages and customs vanish slowly, coins vanish at once.
normal.cn: 语言与风俗消失得慢，硬币却是立刻就没了。

normal.en: Vanish from sight means the eye loses it, not that it never existed.
normal.cn: vanish from sight 指眼睛看不见了，而不是它从未存在。

abstract.en: The word keeps pointing at a hole: something stood here, and now only the outline remains.
abstract.cn: 这个词一直指着那个洞：刚才这里还有东西，如今只剩下轮廓。

abstract.en: Disappearance is a change in the viewer, not always in the thing: vanish describes what the eye reports.
abstract.cn: 消失有时是观看者的变化而非事物的变化：这个词记录的是眼睛的报告。

abstract.en: A word built on emptiness can describe magic, extinction and debt with one motion of the hand.
abstract.cn: 一个以「空」为根的词，用一个挥手的动作就能讲魔术、灭绝与破产。

examples.en: The sun vanished behind the clouds.
examples.cn: 太阳消失在云层后面。

examples.en: He vanished into the crowd before anyone could stop him.
examples.cn: 还没人拦住他，他就消失在人群里了。

examples.en: The keys seem to have vanished from the table.
examples.cn: 钥匙好像从桌上消失了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇泥石」——哇，泥石流一来，房子瞬间不见了：消失

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 vanus「空的」及其动词 evanescere「逝去」，经古法语 esvanir 于十四世纪进入英语；同族词有 vanity、evanescent。

sensesIntro.en: Vanish runs from a coin leaving a hand, through magic and extinction, to habits and savings that empty out.
sensesIntro.cn: vanish 从手里飞走的硬币，经魔术与灭绝，到淡出的风俗与归零的存款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object leaves and the place where it stood is suddenly empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：物件离场，它待过的地方突然空了。

branches.en: SIGHT LINE: the eye loses the object at once.
branches.cn: 视觉线：眼睛一下子抓不到物件。

branches.en: STAGE LINE: the hand is shown empty on purpose.
branches.cn: 舞台线：手心故意摊开给人看是空的。

branches.en: EXISTENCE LINE: whole languages and customs quietly go.
branches.cn: 存在线：整门语言与风俗悄然退场。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: the amount falls to zero.
branches.cn: 数值线：数字一下落到零。

branches.en: CONTRAST: vanish is sudden, fade is gradual.
branches.cn: 对照线：vanish 突兀，fade 渐缓。

intro.en: Vanish carries a Latin root for emptiness plus English verb endings; its relatives hide in common words.
intro.cn: vanish 带一个表示「空」的拉丁词根和英语动词词尾，它的亲属藏在常见词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vanus, empty, with the verb evanescere behind the first syllable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vanus「空的」，开头的 e- 则来自动词 evanescere。

items.example: It carries the core of vanish.
items.exampleCN: 它承载 vanish 的核心义。

items.example: It forms evanescere, to pass out of sight.
It uses the word in art.

definition_zh: 刺穿；扎透；穿透；划破（寂静）；刺骨；深深触动
definition_en: to make a hole in something with a sharp point, or to cut sharply through a surface, a silence or a feeling
core_image: 一根细针从布面这头进、那头出，布上留下一个能被看见的小孔
scene: 深夜的病房里，走廊尽头忽然传来一声尖锐的哭喊，把原本的安静整块切开。 A single cry pierced the stillness of the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里是「划破、穿透」（第 2 个义项：声音或光线强行穿过原本完整的空间）；句意为一声哭喊划破了走廊的寂静。画面里是声音像针一样扎进安静的那一下。

pos.zh: 刺穿；扎透；穿透；划破；刺骨；深深触动

derivatives.zh: 由 pierce 加 -ing 构成，形容声音、目光或寒风「尖锐刺人的」
由 pierce 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，指钻孔的工具或做穿孔工序的人
由 piercing 加 -ly 构成，义为「尖锐地；刺骨地」

senses.title: To make a hole with a sharp point
senses.definition: to push a sharp object into or through something so that it makes a hole
senses.definitionCN: 用尖锐的物体扎入或穿过某物，形成一个小孔
senses.example: The needle pierced the cloth cleanly.
senses.exampleCN: 针干净利落地穿过了布。
senses.why: Old French percer already meant to bore through, and behind it stands Latin pertundere, to beat a hole through something, so the image is a point forcing a passage rather than a light touch.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 percer 本就有钻孔、穿透之意，它背后是拉丁语 pertundere（把某物敲穿），所以这个词的底子是一个尖点硬开出一条通路，而不是轻轻擦过。

senses.title: To cut sharply through silence, light or air
senses.definition: to sound or shine so sharply that it seems to cut through the surrounding space
senses.definitionCN: 声音或光线极其尖锐，仿佛把周围的空间切开
senses.example: A siren pierced the fog above the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一声警笛刺破了港口上方的雾。
senses.why: Once a point can pass through cloth, the same verb is lent to anything that crosses a whole space in one stroke, and sound and light are the things that cross a room fastest.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个尖点能穿过布，这个动词就被借去说任何一下子横穿整片空间的东西；声音和光横穿一间屋子最快，所以最先被借走，划破寂静的用法由此而来。

senses.title: To force its way in, as cold or a gaze does
senses.definition: to enter or reach someone in a sharp, penetrating way, said of cold, wind or a look
senses.definitionCN: 以尖锐、深入的方式进入或触及某人，多就寒冷、风或目光而言
senses.example: The wind pierced her thin coat within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟之内，风就扎透了她的薄外套。
senses.why: Cold and glances enter a body without any tool, yet the sensation is the same as a point going in, so the verb spreads from objects to sensations that behave like objects.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷和目光并没有带上任何工具，却同样钻进身体，感觉与一个尖点扎进去毫无二致，于是这个词从实物扩展到行为像实物的感受。

senses.title: To wound or move someone deeply
senses.definition: to affect someone with sudden sharp emotion, as if something had gone through them
senses.definitionCN: 以突然而尖锐的情绪击中某人，仿佛有东西穿过了他
senses.example: Her question pierced him more than any insult.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个问题比任何辱骂都更刺痛他。
senses.why: The physical hole becomes a hole in someone's composure: what enters is no longer a needle but a sentence, and the wound is felt without ever being seen.
senses.whyCN: 实物上的孔变成了一个人镇定上的孔：扎进去的不再是针，而是一句话，伤口感觉得到却始终看不见，这正是从刺穿到刺心的那一转。

intro.en: Pierce comes through Old French percer from a Latin verb of boring, and the whole family keeps the picture of a point beating its way through material.
intro.cn: pierce 经古法语 percer 上溯到一个表示钻孔的拉丁动词，整族词都保留着尖点把材料一点点打开的画面。

items.en: Tundere meant to beat or to strike, and it underlies a set of Latin verbs about hammering and pounding.
items.cn: tundere 意为敲打、击打，一整组表示锤击、舂打的拉丁动词都由它构成。

items.en: Adding per-, through, produced pertundere, to beat or bore a hole through something.
items.cn: 加上表示穿过的 per-，构成 pertundere，意为把某物敲穿、钻透。

items.en: The recorded route runs through a Vulgar Latin verb pertusiare, to pierce; it is generally taken as the reconstructed link to the French form.
items.cn: 有记录的路径经过俗拉丁语动词 pertusiare（刺穿）；一般认为它是通往法语形式的中间环节，属于重构形式。

items.en: Old French percer meant to bore through and was carried into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 percer 意为钻孔、穿透，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English had the verb by the thirteenth century, first about weapons and wounds, later about sound, cold and feeling.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪已有这个动词，最初说武器与伤口，后来才用于声音、寒冷与情绪。

note.en: The first group gathers words with the same Latin boring root or a nearly identical look; the second gathers verbs of cutting into, entering and passing through.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁「钻孔」词根的词以及外形极近的词；第二组收表示扎入、进入与穿过的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun built from the verb, naming a sharp sound or a hole worn for jewellery.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个动词派生的形容词与名词，指尖锐的声音，或为戴饰品而穿的孔。

entries.definition: A platform built out over water for boats to moor; the spelling is close but the word has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 伸到水面上供船只停靠的平台；拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Violent and angry; only the opening letters differ, and the two words share no history.
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛愤怒的；只有开头几个字母不同，两词并无共同来源。

entries.definition: To make one or more holes through a surface, built on per- and a Latin verb of boring.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物表面打出一个或多个孔，由 per- 与表示钻孔的拉丁动词构成。

entries.definition: To push a knife or other pointed thing into a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 用刀或其他尖物扎入人或动物体内。

entries.definition: To go into or through something, often against resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 进入或穿过某物，常带克服阻力的意味。

entries.definition: To make a small hole in something such as a tyre or a skin.
entries.definitionCN: 在轮胎、皮肤等物体上扎出小孔。

entries.definition: To make a deep round hole with a tool that turns.
entries.definitionCN: 用旋转的工具钻出深的圆孔。

normalIntro.en: A Latin verb of beating and a French verb of boring meet in one word, and every sense still carries a point that opens a way.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「敲打」与法语的「钻孔」在同一个词里会合，每个义项都还带着一个把路打开的尖点。

normal.en: Per- means through and tundere means to beat, so to pierce is literally to beat a way through the material.
normal.cn: per- 意为穿过，tundere 意为敲打，所以 pierce 字面上就是把材料敲出一条通路。

normal.en: French percer dropped the Latin t and softened the ending, which is why English has pierce and not the longer Latin shape.
normal.cn: 法语 percer 丢掉了拉丁语的 t，又软化了词尾，英语因此得到 pierce，而不是那个更长的拉丁词形。

normal.en: The past tense and past participle are both pierced, with no doubling of the r and no change of vowel.
normal.cn: 过去式与过去分词都是 pierced，r 不双写，元音也不变。

normal.en: The -ing form leads a double life: as a participle it describes the action, as an adjective it describes a sound that seems to cut.
normal.cn: 加 -ing 的形式有双重身份：作分词时叙述动作，作形容词时形容一种仿佛会切割的声音。

normal.en: A pierced ear, a piercing cry and a piercing wind all keep the one image of something going straight through.
normal.cn: 打了耳洞的耳朵、刺耳的哭喊、刺骨的风，都守着同一个画面：有东西直穿而过。

abstract.en: A needle leaves a hole too small to see, yet the cloth is no longer whole; pierce names exactly that invisible change.
abstract.cn: 针留下的孔小得看不见，布却已经不完整；pierce 命名的正是这种看不见的改变。

abstract.en: A sound cuts nothing, but we say it pierces because attention is a fabric, and a loud noise tears it along one line.
abstract.cn: 声音其实什么也切不开，我们却说它刺穿，是因为注意力像一块布，巨响沿着一条线把它撕开。

abstract.en: The word travels from metal to voice to feeling, which shows how readily English gives pain and noise a sharp point.
abstract.cn: 这个词从金属走到声音，再走到感情，说明英语多愿意给痛感和噪音装上一个尖点。

examples.en: The arrow pierced the target just outside the ring.
examples.cn: 箭射穿了靶面，落在环外一点。

examples.en: A piercing whistle came from the far end of the platform.
examples.cn: 站台尽头传来一声刺耳的哨响。

examples.en: Nothing he said pierced her calm that afternoon.
examples.cn: 那天下午他说什么也没能刺破她的平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮儿撕」——针尖把皮儿一撕就透，像扎穿布面；pierce 就是刺穿、扎透。

root: 古法语 percer（钻孔、穿透）一般认为来自俗拉丁语 pertusiare，其源头是拉丁语 pertundere（per- 穿过 + tundere 敲打）；同族词多与打孔、贯穿有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts from a point making a hole and then lends that point to sound, to cold, to a glance and finally to a sentence that hurts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一个尖点打出一个孔开始，然后把那个尖点借给声音、寒冷、目光，最后借给一句伤人的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine needle entering one side of the cloth and coming out the other, leaving a visible hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细针从布面这头进、那头出，布上留下一个能被看见的小孔。

branches.en: a needle passing through cloth held taut
branches.cn: 针穿过绷紧的布面

branches.en: a siren splitting the fog over the water
branches.cn: 警笛把水面上的雾劈开

branches.en: wind finding the gap at a thin cuff
branches.cn: 风从薄袖口找缝隙钻进去

branches.en: one sentence that ends a cheerful evening
branches.cn: 一句话结束了原本愉快的夜晚

branches.en: a single point opening a way through something whole
branches.cn: 一个尖点在一整片东西上开出通路

intro.en: A Latin prefix of passage, two Latin verbs of beating and boring, a French verb of drilling and an English suffix hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示穿过的拉丁前缀、两个表示敲打与钻孔的拉丁动词、一个表示钻孔的法语动词，以及一个英语后缀，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is recorded through tundere and pertundere; the Vulgar Latin pertusiare is a reconstructed form rather than a directly attested text word.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的拉丁来历可由 tundere 与 pertundere 追到；俗拉丁语 pertusiare 属于重构形式，并非直接见于文本的词。

items.meaning: to bore through, to beat a hole
forming adjectives and nouns from verbs
items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词与名词

definition_zh: 忠诚；忠心；效忠；（对品牌、球队等的）忠实；专一
definition_en: the quality of being faithful to a person, group or cause, and of not abandoning it in hard times
core_image: 一枚旧徽章别在内侧衣襟上，从不示人，也从不取下
scene: 球队降级那年，看台上仍有一批人穿着旧球衣来，季票一张也没退。 Their loyalty survived the season in which the club lost every home match.
sceneCN: 这里 loyalty 指「对某个群体的忠心，不因处境变坏而撤离」（第 1 个义项：对人与群体的忠诚）；句意为他们的忠诚熬过了球队主场全败的那个赛季。可辨识物件：旧球衣、季票、空荡的看台、记分牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 忠诚；忠心；效忠；忠实；专一

senses.title: Faithfulness to a person or group
senses.definition: steady faithfulness to the people one belongs with, kept even when leaving would be easier
senses.definitionCN: 对自己所属之人保持稳定的忠心，即使离开更容易也不离开
senses.example: Their loyalty survived the season in which the club lost every home match.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的忠诚熬过了球队主场全败的那个赛季。
senses.why: The word began in feudal law as the faithfulness a sworn man owed his lord, so its heart is staying when one could go.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是封建法律中宣誓者对领主的忠贞，核心就是「本可以走却留下」。

senses.title: Allegiance to a state or crown
senses.definition: the formal allegiance a citizen or subject owes to a state, flag or monarch
senses.definitionCN: 公民或臣民对国家、旗帜或君主承担的正式效忠
senses.example: New citizens swear loyalty to the constitution, not to a person.
senses.exampleCN: 新公民宣誓效忠的是宪法，而不是某个人。
senses.why: Feudal faithfulness was taken over by the modern state and attached to an institution rather than a lord.
senses.whyCN: 封建的忠贞被现代国家接手，系在制度上而不是系在领主身上。

senses.title: Sticking with an organisation or team
senses.titleCN: 对组织、球队的忠实追随
senses.definition: the attachment of a member or supporter who keeps supporting a body through poor results
senses.definitionCN: 成员或支持者的归属感：即使成绩不佳也继续支持某个团体
senses.example: Season-ticket holders showed a loyalty that no relegation could shake.
senses.exampleCN: 季票持有者表现出一种降级也摇不动的忠诚。
senses.why: Modern membership moved the old sworn bond into clubs, schools and companies, where nobody has sworn anything.
senses.whyCN: 现代的成员身份把古老的宣誓纽带移进俱乐部、学校与公司，而在那里并没有人宣过誓。

senses.title: Fidelity to an idea
senses.definition: attachment to a principle or cause that survives changes in fashion and cost
senses.definitionCN: 对某项原则或事业的坚持，不因风气与代价的改变而放弃
senses.example: Her loyalty to the reform outlasted three leaders who had promised it.
senses.exampleCN: 她对改革的支持比三位承诺改革的人任期都长。
senses.why: Once the object of faithfulness is no longer a person, loyalty becomes consistency of principle.
senses.whyCN: 当忠贞的对象不再是某个人，忠诚就变成原则上的前后一致。

senses.title: Repeated buying from one brand
senses.titleCN: 对某一品牌的消费忠实
senses.definition: in business, a customer's habit of returning to the same brand or shop instead of switching
senses.definitionCN: 商业中指顾客习惯性回到同一品牌或店铺而不转投他家
senses.example: The airline measured loyalty by how often passengers chose it over a cheaper rival.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司用乘客在多选更便宜的对手时仍选它的频率来衡量忠诚度。
senses.why: Marketing borrowed a moral word for a statistical habit, which is why loyalty programmes can be bought.
senses.whyCN: 营销借用一个道德词来描述统计习惯，所以「忠诚计划」是可以买的。

senses.title: Faithfulness in a close relationship
senses.definition: the promise of exclusivity and steadiness between partners
senses.definitionCN: 伴侣之间专一而稳定的承诺
senses.example: He treated loyalty as a daily practice rather than a single promise.
senses.exampleCN: 他把专一当成每天要做的事，而不是一次性的承诺。
senses.why: The oldest personal sense narrows here to the intimacy of a couple, where faithfulness is tested privately.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的对人之义在这里收窄到伴侣的亲密关系，忠贞在私下受到检验。

senses.title: Doing one's duty faithfully
senses.definition: the reliable performance of a role, especially when nobody is watching or rewarding it
senses.definitionCN: 可靠地履行职责，尤其在无人监督或奖赏时
senses.example: The night guard's loyalty was never noticed until the flood came.
senses.exampleCN: 直到洪水来临，人们才注意到夜班守卫的忠于职守。
senses.why: From faithfulness to persons, the word extends to faithfulness to a task and to those the task protects.
senses.whyCN: 从对人的忠贞，这个词延伸到对任务的忠实，以及对任务所护之人的忠实。

senses.title: Competing allegiances
senses.titleCN: 多重而相互冲突的效忠
senses.definition: in the plural, the several claims on a person's faithfulness that may pull in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指一个人所背负的多种效忠要求，它们可能指向不同方向
senses.example: Divided loyalties made the minister's decision impossible to defend.
senses.exampleCN: 两头为难的效忠让这位部长的决定无法自辩。
senses.why: A person can belong to a family, a firm and a country at once, and the plural names the conflict rather than the virtue.
senses.whyCN: 一个人同时属于家庭、公司与国家，复数形式指的是这种冲突，而不是美德本身。

intro.en: Loyalty comes from Old French loialté, from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'. English legal is the same Latin word borrowed later and directly, so loyal and legal are doublets.
intro.cn: loyalty 来自古法语 loialté，源头是拉丁 legalis「法律的」，再上溯为 lex「法律」。英语的 legal 是同一个拉丁词后来直接借入的形式，因此 loyal 与 legal 是同一词根的两次借入。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute. Its origin is uncertain; a link with the verb legere 'to gather, read' is generally mentioned but not proven, so it is a hypothesis rather than a settled derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为法律、法令。其来源不确定；常有人把它与动词 legere「收集、读」联系起来，但这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Legalis meant 'belonging to the law'. In medieval usage it also described someone who keeps the law, and so someone who is faithful to an oath.
items.cn: legalis 意为「属于法律的」。在中世纪用法中，它也形容守法的人，进而形容忠于誓言的人。

items.en: Old French turned legalis into loial, where the sense had already shifted from lawful to faithful, especially faithful to a lord.
items.cn: 古法语把 legalis 变成 loial，词义已从「合法的」转为「忠实的」，尤其指对领主忠实。

items.en: The abstract noun loialte named that faithfulness, and English took it in the fourteenth century for the bond between a sworn man and his lord.
items.cn: 抽象名词 loialte 指这种忠贞，英语在十四世纪借入，用于宣誓者与领主之间的纽带。

items.en: English later borrowed legalis again, directly and unchanged in meaning, producing legal. Loyal and legal therefore look different and mean different things while sharing one Latin source.
items.cn: 英语后来又直接借入 legalis，词义未变，产生了 legal。因此 loyal 与 legal 形貌与含义都不同，却共享同一个拉丁来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the root of lex has no agreed explanation; the connection with the verb for gathering or reading is a common suggestion, not an established fact, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：lex 的词根没有公认解释；与表示「收集、读」的动词之间的关联只是一种常见推测，并非既定事实，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the Latin law root but arrived by a different route; group two holds near synonyms that differ in what the faithfulness is owed to.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「法律」词根、但走了另一条路径的词；第二组是近义说法，区别在于忠诚所指向的对象。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same stem; loyalty is the quality, loyal the description of a person or act that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的形容词；loyalty 是这种品质，loyal 则形容具备它的人或行为。

entries.definition: The same Latin source borrowed later and directly: it concerns what the law permits, not what faithfulness requires.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁来源后来被直接借入：它关乎法律允许什么，而不关乎忠贞要求什么。

entries.definition: Built on the same law noun with a verb for carrying: it names the making of statutes and has nothing to do with devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法律名词加上表示「携带」的动词构成：它指制定法令，与忠贞无关。

entries.definition: The person noun built on loyal; it usually names someone who stays with a government or cause when others leave.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loyal 构成的人物名词；通常指在别人离开时仍留在某政府或事业一边的人。

entries.definition: The keeping of promises and vows, often in marriage or religion; loyalty adds the idea of belonging to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 信守承诺与誓言，多用于婚姻或宗教；loyalty 更强调归属于某个群体。

entries.definition: Formal obligation of loyalty to a state or sovereign; it is public and sworn, while loyalty can be private and unspoken.
entries.definitionCN: 对国家或君主的正式效忠义务；它是公开的、宣誓的，而 loyalty 可以是私下且不言明的。

entries.definition: Faithfulness in a relationship, or exactness in copying; it stresses precision as much as devotion.
entries.definitionCN: 关系中的忠贞，或复制时的精确；它既强调 devotion，也强调准确。

entries.definition: Deep affection and dedication to a person or activity; it is warmer than loyalty and less concerned with obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某活动的深厚感情与投入；它比 loyalty 更温暖，也更不涉及义务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real law root, the real doublet legal, the real commercial phrases and the real adjective family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「法律」词根、真实的双借词 legal、真实的商业说法，以及真实的形容词词族。

normal.en: The root is the Latin word for law, so loyalty began as the faithfulness a sworn man owed under law.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语中表示「法律」的词，所以忠诚最初是宣誓者在法律之下所欠的忠贞。

normal.en: Legal is the same source borrowed a second time, which is why one word is about faithfulness and the other about permission.
normal.cn: legal 是同一来源的第二次借入，因此一个词关乎忠贞，另一个关乎许可。

normal.en: Business phrases mark the modern sense: brand loyalty, customer loyalty, a loyalty programme.
normal.cn: 商业说法标出现代义：品牌忠诚度、客户忠诚度、会员忠诚计划。

normal.en: The family runs loyalty, loyal, loyally, loyalist, disloyal and disloyalty.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 loyalty、loyal、loyally、loyalist、disloyal 与 disloyalty。

normal.en: The plural loyalties names conflicting claims, as in divided loyalties, rather than more of the same virtue.
normal.cn: 复数形式指的是相互冲突的多重效忠，也就是「两头为难」，而不是同一种美德变得更多。

abstract.en: Picture a badge worn inside the lapel where nobody can see it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚徽章别在内侧衣襟上，谁也看不见。

abstract.en: Picture a seat kept empty for years in case someone returns.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空了许多年的座位，只为等某个人回来。

abstract.en: Picture a road walked in the same direction after every other walker has turned back.
abstract.cn: 想象在其他人都折返之后，仍朝同一方向走下去的一条路。

examples.en: The company rewards loyalty with early access rather than cash.
examples.cn: 公司用优先购买权而不是现金来回报忠诚。

examples.en: His loyalty to the department outlasted four directors.
examples.cn: 他对这个部门的忠诚比四任主管都长久。

examples.en: Divided loyalties kept her from speaking at the hearing.
examples.cn: 两头为难的效忠让她在听证会上无法开口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法律之下的守约」——受人以托、守约不弃，就是忠诚

root: 古法语 loialté ← 拉丁 legalis「法律的」← lex「法律」。英语 legal 是同一拉丁词后来的直接借入，故 loyal 与 legal 同源而异貌。lex 的更深词源不确定，与「收集、读」的关联仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a sworn faithfulness to a person, then widen to a state, a team, an idea, a brand, a partner, a duty, and finally to the conflicts that arise when several of these claims meet in one life.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从对某个人的宣誓忠贞开始，再依次扩展到国家、团队、理念、品牌、伴侣、职责，最后落在多重效忠同时压到一个人身上时的冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a badge worn on the inside of a lapel, never shown and never removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚别在内侧衣襟上的徽章，从不示人，也从不取下。

branches.en: PERSONAL BOND: from a sworn man to a partner, faithfulness is tested in private.
branches.cn: 个人纽带：从宣誓者到伴侣，忠贞都在私下受到检验。

branches.en: THE STATE: the old bond is transferred to a constitution or a crown.
branches.cn: 国家：古老的纽带被移交给宪法或王冠。

branches.en: BELONGING AND BUYING: clubs and brands inherit the language of allegiance.
branches.cn: 归属与购买：俱乐部与品牌继承了效忠的语言。

branches.en: CAUSE AND DUTY: when no person is involved, loyalty becomes consistency and reliability.
branches.cn: 事业与职责：当对象不是人，忠诚就变成前后一致与可靠。

branches.en: THE SPLIT: the plural turns the virtue into a dilemma.
branches.cn: 分裂：复数形式把这份美德变成两难。

intro.en: Loyalty is a French abstract noun on a Latin law root, with a suffix that turns an adjective into a quality.
intro.cn: loyalty 是一个建在拉丁「法律」词根上的法语抽象名词，其词尾把形容词变成一种品质。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex supplies the stem, legalis supplies the adjective, and the French ending marks the abstract quality; the same stem also built legal and legislation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex 提供词干，legalis 提供形容词，法语的词尾标出抽象品质；同一词干还造出了 legal 与 legislation。

items.example: The root names the law under which an oath is sworn.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指誓言所依凭的法律。

items.example: The adjective shifted from lawful to faithful.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「合法的」转为「忠实的」。

items.example: A loial man kept his oath to his lord.
items.exampleCN: 忠实的人会守住对领主的誓言。

items.example: Their loyalty survived the season in which the club lost every home match.
items.exampleCN: 他们的忠诚熬过了球队主场全败的那个赛季。

items.example: A loyal reader renews before the deadline.
items.exampleCN: 忠实的读者会在截止前续订。

items.example: He served loyally for thirty years.
items.exampleCN: 他忠诚地服务了三十年。

items.example: The loyalists refused to leave the building.
items.exampleCN: 效忠者拒绝离开那栋楼。

items.example: The court treated silence as disloyalty.

definition_zh: 殖民地；聚居群体；群落
definition_en: a country or area controlled by another country, a group of people living together, or a group of the same animals or plants in one place
core_image: 远方土地上，一批外来者建起的整齐定居点
scene: 海边的礁石上密密麻麻爬满了同类的小生物。 A colony of ants moved across the kitchen floor.
sceneCN: 这里 colony 指「聚居群体」（第 2 个义项：同类聚在一处）；句意是一群蚂蚁爬过厨房地面。

pos.zh: 殖民地；聚居群体；生物群落

senses.title: A controlled territory
senses.definition: a country or area ruled by another country that settled there
senses.definitionCN: 由他国统治并在那里定居的地区
senses.example: The island was once a colony.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛曾是殖民地。
senses.why: The Latin word named a settlement of farmers far from home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指远离家乡的农人定居点。

senses.title: A group living together
senses.definition: a group of people of one kind living in the same place
senses.definitionCN: 同类人聚居在同一地方形成的群体
senses.example: A colony of painters took over the old street.
senses.exampleCN: 一群画家占据了那条老街。
senses.why: Any settlement of like people kept the old farming image.
senses.whyCN: 任何同类人的聚居都沿用了旧日农耕定居的画面。

senses.title: A group of organisms
senses.definition: a group of the same kind of animals or plants living in one area
senses.definitionCN: 同一类动植物生活在同一区域的群体
senses.example: The reef supports a large colony of crabs.
senses.exampleCN: 这片礁石养活了一个很大的蟹群。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word because ants settle like farmers.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，因为蚂蚁像农夫一样定居。

intro.en: Colony comes from Latin colonia, a settlement of farmers, from colere, to cultivate.
intro.cn: colony 出自拉丁语 colonia（农人定居点），源头是 colere（耕作）。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil and to dwell.
items.cn: colere 意为耕作土地与居住。

items.en: Colonus was a farmer who worked the land.
items.cn: colonus 是耕种土地的农人。

items.en: Colonia named a settlement of such farmers abroad.
items.cn: colonia 指这类农人在外建立的定居点。

items.en: English colony described overseas settlements.
items.cn: 英语 colony 描述海外定居点。

items.en: Science applied it to groups of animals and plants.
items.cn: 科学把它用于动植物群体。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the spelling, while the meaning group names settlements, land and living groups.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写相近的词，近义组列出定居点、土地与聚居群体。

entries.definition: a light perfume named after a German city
entries.definitionCN: 以德国城市命名的淡香水

entries.definition: a high rank in the army
entries.definitionCN: 军队中的高级军衔

entries.definition: a tall stone post or a regular newspaper piece
entries.definitionCN: 高石柱或报纸的定期专栏

entries.definition: a place where people have made their home
entries.definitionCN: 人们安家落户的地方

entries.definition: land under the control of a state
entries.definitionCN: 由国家控制的土地

entries.definition: a group of people living in one place
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活在一处的群体

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with farmers settling new land, then widen to any group that lives together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从农人开垦新地开始，再扩展到任何聚居的群体。

normal.en: Colony hides the Latin colere, to cultivate the soil.
normal.cn: colony 里藏着拉丁语 colere（耕作土地）。

normal.en: A colony began as farmers' fields, not as a government office.
normal.cn: 殖民地最初是一片农田，而不是一间衙门。

normal.en: Ants build a colony in the same way farmers build a village.
normal.cn: 蚂蚁建立群落，就像农人建立村庄。

normal.en: Colonial is the adjective, colonist the person, colonize the act.
normal.cn: colonial 是形容词，colonist 是人，colonize 是动作。

normal.en: The plural colonies changes y into ies.
normal.cn: 复数 colonies 把词尾 y 变成 ies。

abstract.en: Picture a neat row of new houses on an empty coast.
abstract.cn: 想象空旷海岸上一排整齐的新房。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every window shows a painter at work.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，每扇窗里都有画家在工作。

abstract.en: Picture a stone alive with hundreds of small shells.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头上爬满数百只小贝壳。

examples.en: The country gained independence from its former colony.
examples.cn: 这个国家从它的前殖民地获得了独立。

examples.en: An ant colony can build a city under a stone.
examples.cn: 一个蚁群能在石头下建起一座城。

examples.en: A colony of gulls nested on the far rocks.
examples.cn: 一群海鸥在远处的礁石上筑巢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 colony 记成 colere 开垦出来的地方：先是一片田，后来是一群人。

root: 源自拉丁语 colonia（农人定居点），由 colere（耕作、居住）派生，后指殖民地、聚居群体与生物群落。

sensesIntro.en: From tilled fields abroad to any group of people or creatures living in one place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从海外开垦的田地，到任何在一处生活的同类人或生物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young settlement of newcomers on distant soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：在远方土地上由新来者建立的定居点。

branches.en: The political sense grew from overseas farming settlements.
branches.cn: 政治义从海外农耕定居点生长出来。

branches.en: Any like-minded group living together can be a colony.
branches.cn: 任何志趣相投、聚居一处的群体都可称 colony。

branches.en: Biology borrows the word for ants, bees and seabirds.
branches.cn: 生物学借这个词指蚂蚁、蜜蜂与海鸟。

branches.en: Both senses describe people gathered in a new place.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述人聚在新地方。

branches.en: People and animals both settle in groups of their own kind.
branches.cn: 人与动物都会按同类聚成群体定居。

intro.en: The family grows from the root colere, with -ial, -ist and -ize forming its main words.
intro.cn: 这个词族从词根 colere 生长，-ial、-ist 与 -ize 构成主要成员。

latinIntro.en: Colonia and colere are the Latin sources, and culture shares the same root.
latinIntro.cn: colonia 与 colere 是拉丁语来源，culture 也共享同一词根。

items.meaningCN: 多块殖民地或多个群落
items.example: The bird colonies line the northern cliffs.
items.exampleCN: 鸟群沿北面的悬崖分布。

items.meaning: relating to a colony or its ruler
items.meaningCN: 与殖民地或其统治者有关的
items.example: The town keeps its colonial houses.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子保留着殖民地时期的房屋。

items.meaning: a person who settles in a new colony
items.example: Each colonist received a plot of land.
items.exampleCN: 每位定居者分到一块土地。

items.meaning: to settle and control a new area
items.meaningCN: 在新的地区定居并控制它
items.example: Birds colonize the island every spring.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类每年春天到这个岛上定居。

items.meaningCN: 被外来者定居并控制的
items.example: The coast was colonized long ago.
items.exampleCN: 这片海岸很久以前就被殖民了。

items.meaning: the process of settling a new area
items.example: The book studies the colonization of the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这本书研究该山谷的殖民过程。

items.meaning: the practice of ruling other lands
items.example: The museum examines the history of colonialism.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆审视殖民主义的历史。

items.meaning: supporting the rule of other lands
items.example: The old maps carry a colonialist view.
items.exampleCN: 那些旧地图带有殖民者视角。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 农人在外建立的定居点
latinEntries.example: Colonia is the direct source of colony.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colonia 是 colony 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Colere also lies behind the word culture.
latinEntries.exampleCN: colere 也藏在 culture 一词背后。
